fields.Title: A Trip to the Moon
fields.Cast: Georges Méliès; Bleuette Bernon
fields.Clue: A capsule fired from a giant cannon lands in the eye of a man's face in the sky.
fields.Still caption: The capsule lands in the eye of the Moon
fields.Notes: The work of a stage magician turned filmmaker, shot in his glass studio at Montreuil; a hand-coloured print found in Barcelona in 1993 was restored in 2011.
fields.Still 2 caption: Georges Méliès (left) in his glass studio at Montreuil

fields.Title: Intolerance
fields.Cast: Lillian Gish; Mae Marsh; Constance Talmadge
fields.Clue: Four stories, from the fall of Babylon to a modern strike, are intercut and linked by a woman rocking a cradle.
fields.Still caption: Lillian Gish, the woman who rocks the cradle
fields.Notes: Partly Griffith's answer to the outcry over The Birth of a Nation; it lost so much money that its Babylon set stood decaying beside Sunset Boulevard for years.
fields.Still 2 caption: The Babylon set, with elephants on its columns
fields.Still 3 caption: The fall of Babylon

fields.Title: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari
fields.Cast: Werner Krauss; Conrad Veidt
fields.Clue: A fairground showman exhibits a sleepwalker named Cesare and sends him out at night to murder.
fields.Notes: The frame story was added over the writers' objections; its warped sets are the founding image of German Expressionist cinema.
fields.Still 2 caption: Cesare on the painted rooftops of Holstenwall
fields.Still 3 caption: Werner Krauss as Dr. Caligari

fields.Title: Battleship Potemkin
fields.Cast: Aleksandr Antonov; Vladimir Barsky
fields.Clue: Sailors mutiny over maggot-ridden meat, and the citizens who cheer them are cut down by troops on a long flight of steps.
fields.Notes: The Odessa Steps massacre never happened, but the sequence is the standard demonstration of Eisenstein's theory of montage.

fields.Title: Sunrise
fields.Original title: Sunrise: A Song of Two Humans
fields.Cast: George O'Brien; Janet Gaynor
fields.Clue: A farmer is talked by a woman from the city into drowning his wife, cannot go through with it, and falls in love with her again.
fields.Still caption: George O'Brien and Margaret Livingston, the woman from the city
fields.Notes: F. W. Murnau's first American film; it won the only Academy Award ever given for Unique and Artistic Production, at the first ceremony.

fields.Title: Metropolis
fields.Cast: Brigitte Helm; Alfred Abel; Gustav Fröhlich
fields.Clue: An inventor builds a robot double of the saintly Maria to incite the workers who toil beneath a city of the future.
fields.Still caption: Brigitte Helm on set as the Maschinenmensch
fields.Notes: Written by Thea von Harbou, it ends on the moral that the heart must mediate between the head and the hands; a nearly complete print was found in Buenos Aires in 2008.
fields.Still 2 caption: The Maschinenmensch brought to life
fields.Still 3 caption: Rotwang shows Joh Fredersen the Maschinenmensch

fields.Title: The Passion of Joan of Arc
fields.Cast: Renée Falconetti; Antonin Artaud
fields.Clue: A trial and a burning are compressed into a single day, shot almost entirely in huge close-ups of faces against bare white walls.
fields.Notes: Renée Falconetti's only film role; the original negative burned, and a complete print turned up in 1981 in a closet of a Norwegian mental hospital.
fields.Still 2 caption: Renée Falconetti, shot from below; Dreyer dug holes in the set for the low angles

fields.Title: The Blue Angel
fields.Cast: Marlene Dietrich; Emil Jannings
fields.Clue: A respectable schoolmaster is ruined by his infatuation with a cabaret singer, and ends as a clown crowing like a rooster.
fields.Still caption: Marlene Dietrich as Lola Lola
fields.Notes: It made Marlene Dietrich a star with “Falling in Love Again”; it was shot twice, in German and in English.
fields.Still 2 caption: Marlene Dietrich in her cabaret pose

fields.Title: People on Sunday
fields.Director: Robert Siodmak and Edgar G. Ulmer
fields.Cast: Erwin Splettstößer; Brigitte Borchert
fields.Clue: Four young Berliners with no acting experience spend their day off at the Wannsee lakes, and almost nothing happens.
fields.Notes: Billy Wilder wrote it and Fred Zinnemann assisted on camera; nearly everyone involved had fled Germany within three years.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Robert Siodmak and Edgar G. Ulmer, 1930

fields.Title: City Lights
fields.Cast: Charlie Chaplin; Virginia Cherrill
fields.Clue: The Tramp is mistaken for a millionaire by a blind flower girl, and pays for the operation that restores her sight.
fields.Notes: Released without dialogue four years into the sound era; Chaplin shot the first meeting 342 times, and the closing close-up is often called the greatest in cinema.
fields.Still 2 caption: The Tramp meets the blind flower girl

fields.Title: M
fields.Cast: Peter Lorre; Otto Wernicke
fields.Clue: A child murderer who whistles “In the Hall of the Mountain King” is hunted down and tried by the city's own criminals.
fields.Notes: Peter Lorre's first major role, and Lang's first sound film; a beggar marks the killer with a chalk letter pressed onto his shoulder.

fields.Title: Duck Soup
fields.Cast: Groucho Marx; Harpo Marx; Chico Marx; Margaret Dumont
fields.Clue: Rufus T. Firefly becomes the leader of Freedonia and blunders into war with neighbouring Sylvania.
fields.Still caption: Groucho Marx and Margaret Dumont
fields.Notes: The Marx Brothers' last film for Paramount, and a flop; it contains the mirror scene, in which two men in identical nightshirts mimic each other.
fields.Still 2 caption: Groucho Marx in one of his costumes from the war sequence

fields.Title: King Kong
fields.Director: Merian C. Cooper and Ernest B. Schoedsack
fields.Cast: Fay Wray; Robert Armstrong; Bruce Cabot
fields.Clue: A giant ape is taken from Skull Island to New York, where he breaks his chains and climbs the Empire State Building.
fields.Still caption: Kong sets Ann Darrow (Fay Wray) in a tree before fighting a Tyrannosaurus
fields.Notes: Willis O'Brien animated him in stop motion; the closing line blames beauty for killing the beast.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Merian C. Cooper and Ernest B. Schoedsack, 1933
fields.Still 2 caption: A colour publicity image combining live actors with stop-motion animation
fields.Still 3 caption: The producer Merian C. Cooper with the full-size mechanical head used for close-ups

fields.Title: Zero for Conduct
fields.Cast: Jean Dasté; Robert le Flon
fields.Clue: Boys at a repressive boarding school stage a revolt after a slow-motion pillow fight fills their dormitory with feathers.
fields.Notes: Jean Vigo made it at 28, and France banned it until 1945; it was the direct model for Lindsay Anderson's If....

fields.Title: The Bride of Frankenstein
fields.Cast: Boris Karloff; Elsa Lanchester; Ernest Thesiger
fields.Clue: Dr. Pretorius, who keeps homunculi in jars, forces his old colleague to build the monster a mate, who hisses at him.
fields.Still caption: Boris Karloff as the Monster
fields.Notes: Elsa Lanchester plays both the mate and Mary Shelley in the prologue; it is widely thought better than the 1931 original.
fields.Still 2 caption: Elsa Lanchester as the Monster's mate
fields.Still 3 caption: Boris Karloff, James Whale, and the cinematographer John J. Mescall on set

fields.Title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
fields.Cast: Adriana Caselotti; Lucille La Verne
fields.Clue: Disney's first feature film, known around Hollywood during production as “Disney's Folly.”
fields.Notes: The first full-length cel-animated feature in English; its honorary Oscar was one full-size statuette and seven miniature ones.

fields.Title: The Wizard of Oz
fields.Cast: Judy Garland; Ray Bolger; Bert Lahr; Margaret Hamilton
fields.Clue: A Kansas farm girl is carried by a cyclone into a Technicolor land, where she follows a yellow brick road.
fields.Still caption: Jack Haley, Judy Garland, Ray Bolger, and Bert Lahr as the Tin Man, Dorothy, the Scarecrow, and the Cowardly Lion
fields.Notes: Victor Fleming took over from Richard Thorpe and George Cukor; “Over the Rainbow” was nearly cut, and the slippers were silver in L. Frank Baum's book.
fields.Still 2 caption: Judy Garland as Dorothy
fields.Still 3 caption: Billie Burke as Glinda and Judy Garland as Dorothy

fields.Title: The Rules of the Game
fields.Cast: Marcel Dalio; Nora Gregor; Jean Renoir
fields.Clue: A weekend shooting party at a country château tangles servants and aristocrats in the same adulteries, around a rabbit hunt filmed as a massacre.
fields.Still caption: Nora Gregor, Jean Renoir, Pierre Nay, and Pierre Magnier at the rabbit hunt
fields.Notes: Jean Renoir plays Octave, who says that everyone has their reasons; booed and cut in 1939, it was reconstructed in 1959 and now tops critics' polls.

fields.Title: Gone with the Wind
fields.Cast: Vivien Leigh; Clark Gable; Hattie McDaniel; Olivia de Havilland
fields.Clue: A plantation owner's daughter swears, clutching a radish in the ruins of Tara, that she will never be hungry again.
fields.Still caption: Clark Gable and Vivien Leigh as Rhett and Scarlett
fields.Notes: Hattie McDaniel became the first Black performer to win an Academy Award; adjusted for inflation, it is still the highest-grossing film ever made.
fields.Still 2 caption: Vivien Leigh and Hattie McDaniel as Scarlett and Mammy

fields.Title: His Girl Friday
fields.Cast: Cary Grant; Rosalind Russell; Ralph Bellamy
fields.Clue: A newspaper editor schemes to keep his ex-wife, his star reporter, from remarrying by handing her one last story on the eve of an execution.
fields.Still caption: Cary Grant, Rosalind Russell, and Ralph Bellamy in a publicity photograph
fields.Notes: An adaptation of The Front Page with the reporter Hildy Johnson rewritten as a woman; the dialogue overlaps so fast that extra lines were written to be talked over.
fields.Still 2 caption: Cary Grant and Rosalind Russell (right)
fields.Still 3 caption: Cary Grant and Rosalind Russell, in a costume by Robert Kalloch

fields.Title: Citizen Kane
fields.Cast: Orson Welles; Joseph Cotten; Dorothy Comingore
fields.Clue: A reporter tries to learn what a dying newspaper tycoon meant by his last word, “Rosebud.”
fields.Still caption: Kane shouts down the stairs after the departing Boss Jim W. Gettys
fields.Notes: Gregg Toland shot it in deep focus for a 25-year-old first-time director; William Randolph Hearst tried to have the negative destroyed.
fields.Still 2 caption: Orson Welles and Ruth Warrick in the breakfast montage

fields.Title: Casablanca
fields.Cast: Humphrey Bogart; Ingrid Bergman; Claude Rains; Paul Henreid
fields.Clue: A cynical American nightclub owner in Vichy Morocco gives up two letters of transit to a Czech resistance leader and the woman they both love.
fields.Still caption: Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman in the airport scene
fields.Notes: The script was still being written during shooting, and the last line about a beautiful friendship was dubbed in afterwards; “Play it again, Sam” is never said.
fields.Still 2 caption: Paul Henreid, Ingrid Bergman, and Humphrey Bogart
fields.Still 3 caption: Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman

fields.Title: To Be or Not to Be
fields.Cast: Carole Lombard; Jack Benny; Robert Stack
fields.Clue: A Warsaw theatre troupe uses its costumes and its ham acting to outwit the Gestapo.
fields.Still caption: Carole Lombard in a publicity still
fields.Notes: Carole Lombard was killed in a plane crash before its release, and in 1942 it was attacked for joking about the occupation.

fields.Title: Ossessione
fields.Cast: Clara Calamai; Massimo Girotti
fields.Clue: A drifter and a roadhouse owner's wife murder her husband in the Po valley, in an unlicensed version of The Postman Always Rings Twice.
fields.Notes: Luchino Visconti's first feature, usually counted the first Neorealist film; the rights problem kept it unseen in the United States until 1976.

fields.Title: Laura
fields.Cast: Gene Tierney; Dana Andrews; Clifton Webb
fields.Clue: A detective investigating a woman's murder falls in love with her portrait, and then she walks through the door alive.
fields.Still caption: Dana Andrews as Detective Mark McPherson
fields.Notes: David Raksin's theme became a standard; Clifton Webb's columnist Waldo Lydecker was modelled on Alexander Woollcott.
fields.Still 2 caption: Clifton Webb, Gene Tierney, and Vincent Price in the trailer
fields.Still 3 caption: Gene Tierney in a publicity photograph

fields.Title: Children of Paradise
fields.Cast: Arletty; Jean-Louis Barrault; Pierre Brasseur
fields.Clue: A mime, an actor, a criminal, and an aristocrat love the same woman along the Boulevard du Crime in 1830s Paris.
fields.Notes: Shot in occupied France while its Jewish designer, Alexandre Trauner, and composer, Joseph Kosma, worked in hiding; often voted the greatest French film.

fields.Title: Beauty and the Beast
fields.Cast: Jean Marais; Josette Day
fields.Clue: Living arms hold candelabra along the corridors of an enchanted castle, where stone faces follow the heroine with their eyes.
fields.Notes: An opening title asks the audience for a child's simple faith; Jean Marais plays three roles.

fields.Title: A Matter of Life and Death
fields.Cast: David Niven; Kim Hunter; Roger Livesey
fields.Clue: An RAF pilot who bails out without a parachute survives through a clerical error in the afterlife, and must argue his case before a celestial court.
fields.Still caption: Marius Goring, David Niven, Roger Livesey, Kim Hunter, and Robert Coote
fields.Notes: Earth is in Technicolor and the other world in monochrome; the Foreign Office asked for it, to improve Anglo-American relations.
fields.Poster caption: Poster · Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger, 1946
fields.Still 2 caption: Marius Goring as Conductor 71 and David Niven as Peter Carter

fields.Title: It's a Wonderful Life
fields.Cast: James Stewart; Donna Reed; Lionel Barrymore
fields.Clue: An apprentice angel shows a despairing building-and-loan manager what Bedford Falls would have become without him.
fields.Still caption: James Stewart and Gloria Grahame as George Bailey and Violet Bick
fields.Notes: It flopped on release and became a Christmas fixture only after its copyright lapsed in 1974, letting television run it free.
fields.Still 2 caption: The run on the Bailey Building and Loan
fields.Still 3 caption: James Stewart, Donna Reed, and Karolyn Grimes as George, Mary, and Zuzu Bailey

fields.Title: Bicycle Thieves
fields.Cast: Lamberto Maggiorani; Enzo Staiola
fields.Clue: A bill-poster has the means of transport his new job depends on stolen on his first morning, and searches Rome for it with his small son.
fields.Notes: Vittorio De Sica cast non-professionals throughout, the lead a factory worker; it won an honorary Oscar before the foreign-language category existed.

fields.Title: Kind Hearts and Coronets
fields.Cast: Dennis Price; Alec Guinness; Joan Greenwood
fields.Clue: A draper's assistant murders his way through eight relatives, all played by Alec Guinness, to inherit a dukedom.
fields.Still caption: Alec Guinness in six of his eight roles, with Valerie Hobson (second from left)
fields.Notes: He narrates from the condemned cell; American censors demanded an added ending in which his memoirs are found.

fields.Title: The Third Man
fields.Cast: Joseph Cotten; Orson Welles; Alida Valli; Trevor Howard
fields.Clue: A pulp novelist in occupied Vienna learns that his supposedly dead friend is alive and selling diluted penicillin.
fields.Notes: Graham Greene wrote it and Anton Karas's zither scores it; Orson Welles added the speech about Switzerland and the cuckoo clock himself.

fields.Title: Rashomon
fields.Cast: Toshiro Mifune; Machiko Kyō; Masayuki Mori
fields.Clue: A bandit, a samurai's wife, the dead samurai speaking through a medium, and a woodcutter give incompatible accounts of the same killing.
fields.Notes: Its Golden Lion at Venice in 1951 opened Japanese cinema to the West; the title has become a term for irreconcilable accounts of one event.

fields.Title: Sunset Boulevard
fields.Cast: Gloria Swanson; William Holden; Erich von Stroheim
fields.Clue: A screenwriter narrates his story while floating dead in the swimming pool of a forgotten silent star who is ready for her close-up.
fields.Notes: Gloria Swanson really was a silent star, and Erich von Stroheim, who plays her butler, really had directed her.
fields.Still 2 caption: Gloria Swanson and William Holden
fields.Still 3 caption: Norma Desmond’s last scene, before the newsreel cameras

fields.Title: A Streetcar Named Desire
fields.Cast: Marlon Brando; Vivien Leigh; Kim Hunter
fields.Clue: A fading Southern belle moves in with her sister and her brutish brother-in-law in New Orleans, and is destroyed.
fields.Notes: Elia Kazan had directed the play on Broadway; it was Marlon Brando's film breakthrough, and the Production Code cuts were restored only in 1993.

fields.Title: The Night of the Hunter
fields.Cast: Robert Mitchum; Shelley Winters; Lillian Gish
fields.Clue: A murderous preacher with LOVE and HATE tattooed on his knuckles pursues two children down the Ohio River.
fields.Still caption: Robert Mitchum as the preacher Harry Powell, with Shelley Winters
fields.Notes: The only film the actor Charles Laughton directed; it failed so completely that he never directed again.
fields.Still 2 caption: Stanley Cortez's expressionist lighting in the bedroom scene

fields.Title: Singin' in the Rain
fields.Cast: Gene Kelly; Debbie Reynolds; Donald O'Connor
fields.Clue: A studio's changeover to sound is nearly wrecked by its leading lady's voice, so a chorus girl secretly dubs her.
fields.Notes: Built around Arthur Freed's back catalogue of songs; Debbie Reynolds, not a trained dancer, rehearsed until her feet bled.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Stanley Donen and Gene Kelly, 1952

fields.Title: Tokyo Story
fields.Cast: Chishū Ryū; Chieko Higashiyama; Setsuko Hara
fields.Clue: An elderly couple visit their grown children in the capital, and only their widowed daughter-in-law makes time for them.
fields.Notes: The camera sits at the height of someone kneeling on a tatami mat and hardly moves; Ozu's “pillow shots” of empty rooms punctuate it.
fields.Still 2 caption: Yasujirō Ozu (far right) on set
fields.Still 3 caption: Shūkichi and Tomi on the sea wall at Atami

fields.Title: The Wages of Fear
fields.Cast: Yves Montand; Charles Vanel
fields.Clue: Four desperate men stranded in a Latin American oil town are hired to drive two trucks of nitroglycerine over broken roads to a burning well.
fields.Notes: The first film to win both the Palme d'Or and the Golden Bear; William Friedkin remade it as Sorcerer in 1977.

fields.Title: Godzilla
fields.Cast: Takashi Shimura; Akira Takarada
fields.Clue: A creature woken by hydrogen-bomb testing comes ashore and levels Tokyo, until a scientist uses his oxygen destroyer and dies with its secret.
fields.Still caption: Ogata, Yamada, an old fisherman, Emiko, and Professor Yamane
fields.Notes: Released months after the Lucky Dragon No. 5 incident, with the monster played by a man in a suit; the American version cut the politics and added Raymond Burr.
fields.Still 2 caption: The monster, whose design drew on several dinosaurs

fields.Title: All That Heaven Allows
fields.Cast: Jane Wyman; Rock Hudson; Agnes Moorehead
fields.Clue: A well-off New England widow falls for her much younger gardener, and her grown children buy her a television set for company.
fields.Notes: Rainer Werner Fassbinder remade it as Ali: Fear Eats the Soul and Todd Haynes reworked it as Far from Heaven; the studio-imposed happy ending is deliberately hollow.

fields.Title: Rebel Without a Cause
fields.Cast: James Dean; Natalie Wood; Sal Mineo
fields.Clue: A new boy in town is goaded into a “chickie run” of stolen cars toward a cliff edge, and the night ends at the Griffith Observatory.
fields.Still caption: Jim Stark (James Dean) in police custody
fields.Notes: James Dean died in a car crash a month before its release; Sal Mineo's Plato is often read as the first gay teenager in American film.
fields.Still 2 caption: Jim confronts his father as his mother watches

fields.Title: Pather Panchali
fields.Cast: Subir Banerjee; Karuna Banerjee; Chunibala Devi
fields.Clue: A Bengali village boy and his sister run through a field of white kaash flowers to see a train go by.
fields.Notes: The first part of the Apu Trilogy, shot on weekends over three years with an amateur crew; Ravi Shankar wrote the score in a single night.
fields.Still 2 caption: Apu and Durga run to see the train
fields.Still 3 caption: A still shown in the MoMA's 1955 exhibition The Family of Man

fields.Title: Kiss Me Deadly
fields.Cast: Ralph Meeker; Cloris Leachman; Gaby Rodgers
fields.Clue: A thuggish private eye picks up a barefoot woman on a night road, and ends up chasing a glowing box that should never be opened.
fields.Still caption: The apocalyptic final scene
fields.Notes: The glowing box is the ancestor of the briefcase in Pulp Fiction; the apocalyptic ending was cut from prints for decades.

fields.Title: The Searchers
fields.Cast: John Wayne; Jeffrey Hunter; Natalie Wood
fields.Clue: A Confederate veteran spends five years hunting for his niece, taken by Comanches, meaning to kill her for having lived among them.
fields.Still caption: Natalie Wood as Debbie
fields.Notes: The last shot frames him in a doorway that closes on him; his catchphrase, “That'll be the day,” became a Buddy Holly song.
fields.Still 2 caption: Jeffrey Hunter and John Wayne as Martin Pawley and Ethan Edwards
fields.Still 3 caption: The search party rides through Monument Valley

fields.Title: The Seventh Seal
fields.Cast: Max von Sydow; Bengt Ekerot; Gunnar Björnstrand
fields.Clue: A knight back from the Crusades plays chess with Death on a stony beach to buy time.
fields.Still caption: Bengt Ekerot as Death
fields.Notes: It ends with Death leading a dance along a hilltop; Ingmar Bergman took the chess image from a medieval church painting.
fields.Still 2 caption: The dance of death along the hilltop
fields.Still 3 caption: Death and Antonius Block choose sides for the chess game

fields.Title: Vertigo
fields.Cast: James Stewart; Kim Novak
fields.Clue: A San Francisco detective with a fear of heights remakes a shopgirl in the image of the dead woman he was hired to follow.
fields.Still caption: Kim Novak as Madeleine, in profile at Ernie’s restaurant
fields.Notes: Bernard Herrmann scored it, and the dolly zoom is often named after it; a flop in 1958, it displaced Citizen Kane atop the Sight and Sound poll in 2012.

fields.Title: Ashes and Diamonds
fields.Cast: Zbigniew Cybulski; Ewa Krzyżewska
fields.Clue: On the last day of the war, a young Home Army assassin in dark glasses is ordered to kill a Communist official.
fields.Notes: Zbigniew Cybulski, called the Polish James Dean, died young like him, under a train in 1967.

fields.Title: Some Like It Hot
fields.Cast: Marilyn Monroe; Tony Curtis; Jack Lemmon
fields.Clue: Two Chicago musicians witness the St. Valentine's Day Massacre and flee to Florida disguised in an all-female band.
fields.Still caption: Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon as Josephine and Daphne
fields.Notes: The last line is “Nobody's perfect”; it was shot in black and white because the men's makeup looked ghastly in colour.
fields.Still 2 caption: Tony Curtis as “Shell Oil Junior” and Marilyn Monroe as Sugar
fields.Still 3 caption: Billy Wilder and Marilyn Monroe during filming

fields.Title: The 400 Blows
fields.Cast: Jean-Pierre Léaud; Albert Rémy
fields.Clue: A neglected Paris schoolboy escapes from a reform school, runs to the sea, and turns to the camera in a freeze frame.
fields.Notes: François Truffaut's first feature, which launched the New Wave at Cannes; Antoine Doinel returned in four more films with the same actor.
fields.Still 2 caption: Antoine running toward the sea in the final sequence

fields.Title: La Dolce Vita
fields.Cast: Marcello Mastroianni; Anita Ekberg; Anouk Aimée
fields.Clue: A gossip journalist drifts through seven nights of Roman high life, one of them ending with a starlet wading in the Trevi Fountain.
fields.Notes: Its photographer Paparazzo gave the world the word “paparazzi”; the Vatican newspaper denounced it.

fields.Title: Breathless
fields.Cast: Jean-Paul Belmondo; Jean Seberg
fields.Clue: A petty thief who models himself on Humphrey Bogart shoots a policeman and hides out in Paris with an American girl who sells the Herald Tribune.
fields.Still caption: Jean Seberg and Jean-Paul Belmondo
fields.Notes: Shot handheld in four weeks from an outline by François Truffaut; the jump cuts began as a way to shorten an over-long rough cut.

fields.Title: Saturday Night and Sunday Morning
fields.Cast: Albert Finney; Rachel Roberts; Shirley Anne Field
fields.Clue: A Nottingham lathe operator drinks his wages and has an affair with a workmate's wife, insisting he won't let the bastards grind him down.
fields.Notes: From Alan Sillitoe's novel; the first big hit of British kitchen-sink realism, and the film that made Albert Finney a star.

fields.Title: Last Year at Marienbad
fields.Cast: Delphine Seyrig; Giorgio Albertazzi
fields.Clue: In a baroque hotel of mirrors and clipped hedges, a man insists to a woman that they have met before, and she does not remember.
fields.Still caption: The formal garden, where the guests cast shadows and the trees do not
fields.Notes: Written by Alain Robbe-Grillet; nobody involved agreed on whether the meeting happened, and the matchstick game the guests play is Nim.

fields.Title: La Jetée
fields.Cast: Jean Négrioni; Hélène Chatelain
fields.Clue: Told almost entirely in still photographs, it follows a prisoner sent back in time because of a childhood memory of a woman's face on an airport pier.
fields.Notes: It has exactly one moving shot, of a woman blinking; Terry Gilliam's 12 Monkeys is built on it.

fields.Title: The Umbrellas of Cherbourg
fields.Cast: Catherine Deneuve; Nino Castelnuovo
fields.Clue: Every line is sung as a shop girl's lover is conscripted to Algeria, and they meet again years later at a gas station.
fields.Notes: Michel Legrand's score gave the song “I Will Wait for You”; Catherine Deneuve's singing is dubbed.

fields.Title: Black God, White Devil
fields.Original title: Deus e o Diabo na Terra do Sol
fields.Cast: Geraldo Del Rey; Yoná Magalhães
fields.Clue: A cowhand in the drought-stricken sertão kills his boss and follows first a messianic preacher and then a bandit.
fields.Notes: Glauber Rocha called the movement's style an “aesthetic of hunger”; the bandit is a cangaceiro in the tradition of Lampião.

fields.Title: Dr. Strangelove
fields.Original title: Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb
fields.Cast: Peter Sellers; George C. Scott; Slim Pickens; Sterling Hayden
fields.Clue: A general obsessed with precious bodily fluids launches a nuclear strike that cannot be recalled, and a major rides the bomb down waving his hat.
fields.Still caption: General Buck Turgidson (George C. Scott) imitating a low-flying B-52
fields.Notes: Peter Sellers plays three roles; a custard-pie fight in the War Room was shot and cut.
fields.Still 2 caption: Wing Attack Plan R, fresh from the cockpit safe
fields.Still 3 caption: The War Room and its Big Board

fields.Title: The Sound of Music
fields.Cast: Julie Andrews; Christopher Plummer; Eleanor Parker
fields.Clue: A postulant from a Salzburg abbey becomes governess to a widowed naval captain's seven children, and leads the family over the mountains after the Anschluss.
fields.Still caption: Christopher Plummer and Julie Andrews on location in Salzburg
fields.Notes: Robert Wise's Rodgers and Hammerstein adaptation rescued Twentieth Century-Fox after Cleopatra.

fields.Title: The Battle of Algiers
fields.Cast: Brahim Hadjadj; Jean Martin; Saadi Yacef
fields.Clue: Shot in newsreel style with non-professionals, it reconstructs the FLN's bombing campaign in the Casbah and the French paratroopers' use of torture.
fields.Notes: An opening title insists no documentary footage was used; it was banned in France for five years, and was screened at the Pentagon in 2003.

fields.Title: Chelsea Girls
fields.Cast: Nico; Brigid Berlin; Ondine
fields.Clue: Two reels are projected side by side for over three hours as Factory regulars talk, inject, and argue in hotel rooms.
fields.Still caption: Mary Woronov in the colour reel, beside a black-and-white one
fields.Notes: The first underground film to play commercial cinemas; the sound switches between the reels at the projectionist's discretion, so no two screenings are alike.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Andy Warhol and Paul Morrissey, 1966

fields.Title: Playtime
fields.Cast: Jacques Tati; Barbara Dennek
fields.Clue: A bewildered man in a raincoat and a party of American tourists get lost in a Paris of glass partitions and identical cubicles.
fields.Still caption: Jacques Tati as Monsieur Hulot
fields.Notes: Jacques Tati built a steel-and-glass city for it, nicknamed Tativille, and the cost bankrupted him; the gags are spread across a 70mm frame with no close-ups to point at them.
fields.Still 2 caption: The office set, a maze of cubicles
fields.Still 3 caption: The apartments: cubicles for living, seen from the street

fields.Title: Bonnie and Clyde
fields.Cast: Warren Beatty; Faye Dunaway; Gene Hackman
fields.Clue: Two Depression-era bank robbers rove across Texas and Oklahoma until they are cut down in slow motion at a roadside ambush.
fields.Notes: Pauline Kael's long defence of it in The New Yorker is a landmark of criticism; its violence helped end the Production Code.

fields.Title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
fields.Cast: Keir Dullea; Gary Lockwood; Douglas Rain
fields.Clue: A black monolith appears to apes at a waterhole, and a bone thrown into the air cuts to a satellite.
fields.Notes: The soft-voiced computer HAL 9000 kills the crew and is dismantled singing “Daisy Bell”; Arthur C. Clarke co-wrote it.
fields.Still 2 caption: The zero-gravity effect

fields.Title: The Wild Bunch
fields.Cast: William Holden; Ernest Borgnine; Robert Ryan
fields.Clue: Aging outlaws in 1913 sell stolen rifles to a Mexican general, then walk four abreast into an unwinnable gunfight to rescue one of their own.
fields.Notes: Its carnage is cut at several speeds at once; the opening has children feeding scorpions to ants.
fields.Still 2 caption: Sam Peckinpah sets up the final gunfight at “Agua Verde”

fields.Title: Easy Rider
fields.Cast: Peter Fonda; Dennis Hopper; Jack Nicholson
fields.Clue: Two bikers hide their cocaine money in a fuel tank and ride from Los Angeles to Mardi Gras in New Orleans.
fields.Notes: Made for about $400,000, it took some $60 million and convinced the studios to hand films to young directors; Jack Nicholson plays a drunken lawyer.

fields.Title: Le Boucher
fields.Cast: Stéphane Audran; Jean Yanne
fields.Clue: A village schoolmistress befriends the local butcher, a veteran of Indochina and Algeria, while a murderer is at large.
fields.Notes: Blood drips onto a schoolgirl's sandwich at a picnic; Claude Chabrol called it his most Hitchcockian film.

fields.Title: The Godfather
fields.Cast: Marlon Brando; Al Pacino; James Caan; Robert Duvall
fields.Clue: A Hollywood producer who refuses a favour wakes to find a severed horse's head in his bed.
fields.Notes: Paramount wanted neither Marlon Brando nor Al Pacino nor the period setting; it became the highest-grossing film to that point.
fields.Still 2 caption: James Caan, Marlon Brando, Al Pacino, and John Cazale at the wedding

fields.Title: Aguirre, the Wrath of God
fields.Cast: Klaus Kinski; Helena Rojo
fields.Clue: A Spanish expedition searching the Amazon for El Dorado disintegrates under a mutinous lieutenant who declares himself emperor.
fields.Notes: It ends circling a raft of corpses overrun by monkeys; Werner Herzog and Klaus Kinski threatened to kill each other during the shoot.

fields.Title: The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie
fields.Original title: Le Charme discret de la bourgeoisie
fields.Cast: Fernando Rey; Delphine Seyrig; Stéphane Audran
fields.Clue: Six well-bred friends try again and again to sit down to dinner, and are interrupted every time.
fields.Notes: Between attempts they walk down an empty country road; it won Luis Buñuel the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film.

fields.Title: Don't Look Now
fields.Cast: Julie Christie; Donald Sutherland
fields.Clue: A couple whose daughter drowned in a red coat keep glimpsing a small figure in red in wintry Venice.
fields.Still caption: The red coat, a motif throughout
fields.Notes: Adapted from a Daphne du Maurier story; its love scene, intercut with the couple dressing afterwards, was cut in several countries.

fields.Title: Chinatown
fields.Cast: Jack Nicholson; Faye Dunaway; John Huston
fields.Clue: A Los Angeles detective's fake adultery case leads him to a plot to divert the city's water, and to a far worse family secret.
fields.Notes: Robert Towne wrote it and wanted a happier ending, but Roman Polanski overruled him; the water plot is loosely based on the Owens Valley aqueduct.

fields.Title: Ali: Fear Eats the Soul
fields.Cast: Brigitte Mira; El Hedi ben Salem
fields.Clue: A widowed Munich cleaning woman in her sixties marries a much younger Moroccan guest worker, and everyone around them punishes them for it.
fields.Notes: A deliberate reworking of Douglas Sirk's All That Heaven Allows; Fassbinder shot it in about two weeks.

fields.Title: The Spirit of the Beehive
fields.Cast: Ana Torrent; Fernando Fernán Gómez
fields.Clue: In a Castilian village in 1940, a small girl who has seen Frankenstein at a travelling cinema looks for the monster in an abandoned sheepfold, and finds a wounded fugitive.
fields.Notes: Almost everything political is implied rather than stated, which is how it passed the censor; Ana Torrent was six.

fields.Title: Jaws
fields.Cast: Roy Scheider; Robert Shaw; Richard Dreyfuss
fields.Clue: A resort island's police chief, a marine biologist, and an old fisherman who survived the USS Indianapolis go to sea after a great white shark.
fields.Notes: The mechanical shark kept breaking down, so John Williams's two notes stand in for it; the first film to take $100 million, it created the summer blockbuster.

fields.Title: Picnic at Hanging Rock
fields.Cast: Rachel Roberts; Anne-Louise Lambert
fields.Clue: On St. Valentine's Day 1900, three schoolgirls and a teacher vanish on a volcanic outcrop in Victoria, and nothing is explained.
fields.Notes: The novel's final chapter, which offered an explanation, was published only after the author's death; many viewers still believe the story is true.

fields.Title: Taxi Driver
fields.Cast: Robert De Niro; Jodie Foster; Cybill Shepherd
fields.Clue: An insomniac Vietnam veteran who drives nights in New York shaves his head into a mohawk and shoots his way into a brothel to rescue a twelve-year-old.
fields.Notes: Bernard Herrmann's last score; “You talkin' to me?” was improvised, and John Hinckley Jr. cited the film after shooting Ronald Reagan.

fields.Title: Annie Hall
fields.Cast: Woody Allen; Diane Keaton; Tony Roberts
fields.Clue: A neurotic New York comedian looks back on his failed romance with a singer from Chippewa Falls, and pulls Marshall McLuhan from behind a cinema poster to win an argument.
fields.Notes: It beat Star Wars to Best Picture; the working title was Anhedonia, and Diane Keaton's real surname is Hall.
fields.Still 2 caption: Diane Keaton's Annie Hall look, which set a late-1970s fashion

fields.Title: Star Wars
fields.Original title: Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope
fields.Cast: Mark Hamill; Harrison Ford; Carrie Fisher
fields.Clue: A farm boy on a desert planet finds a message hidden in a droid, and flies a trench run to destroy a moon-sized battle station.
fields.Still caption: Luke, Leia, and Han
fields.Notes: Rescued in the edit by a team including Marcia Lucas, George Lucas's then wife; the merchandising rights the studio let him keep made him a fortune.

fields.Title: Alien
fields.Cast: Sigourney Weaver; Tom Skerritt; Ian Holm
fields.Clue: Something attaches itself to a crewman's face on a distant moon, and later bursts out of his chest at dinner.
fields.Notes: H. R. Giger designed the creature, and the tagline promised that in space no one can hear you scream; Ripley was written without a specified gender.
fields.Still 2 caption: Sigourney Weaver as Ripley, with Jones the cat

fields.Title: Stalker
fields.Cast: Aleksandr Kaidanovsky; Anatoly Solonitsyn
fields.Clue: A guide leads a writer and a scientist through a forbidden, guarded zone toward a room said to grant a person's deepest wish.
fields.Notes: Sepia outside the zone and colour within; the first version was ruined in the lab and reshot from scratch.

fields.Title: Das Boot
fields.Cast: Jürgen Prochnow; Herbert Grönemeyer
fields.Clue: A U-boat crew endures depth charges, survives being pinned on the sea floor below crush depth, and is destroyed in an air raid within sight of home.
fields.Still caption: The officers of U-96
fields.Notes: Shot in a full-size hull on gimbals with the camera racing its length; the actors were kept out of daylight so they would look pale.

fields.Title: Blade Runner
fields.Cast: Harrison Ford; Rutger Hauer; Sean Young
fields.Clue: In a rainy, neon Los Angeles of 2019, a burnt-out policeman hunts four escaped artificial humans with four-year lifespans.
fields.Notes: Rutger Hauer largely wrote the tears-in-rain speech himself; Vangelis scored it, and later cuts dropped the studio's voiceover and happy ending.
fields.Still 2 caption: A police spinner among the skyscrapers

fields.Title: Blue Velvet
fields.Cast: Kyle MacLachlan; Isabella Rossellini; Dennis Hopper
fields.Clue: A college student home in a picture-book American town finds a severed ear in a field.
fields.Notes: Dennis Hopper plays a gas-huffing psychopath; Roger Ebert loathed the film and Pauline Kael championed it.

fields.Title: Wings of Desire
fields.Cast: Bruno Ganz; Solveig Dommartin; Peter Falk
fields.Clue: Angels in overcoats listen to the thoughts of Berliners, until one falls in love with a trapeze artist and chooses to become mortal.
fields.Notes: The angels see in black and white; Peter Falk plays himself, a former angel, and Peter Handke wrote much of the text.

fields.Title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown
fields.Original title: Mujeres al borde de un ataque de nervios
fields.Cast: Carmen Maura; Antonio Banderas; Julieta Serrano
fields.Clue: A dubbing actress abandoned by her lover spikes a batch of gazpacho with sleeping pills while her flat fills with his son, his fiancée, and his mad ex-wife.
fields.Notes: It made Pedro Almodóvar an international name and was nominated for the foreign-language Oscar; Antonio Banderas plays the son.

fields.Title: Sex, Lies, and Videotape
fields.Cast: James Spader; Andie MacDowell; Laura San Giacomo
fields.Clue: An impotent drifter who videotapes women talking about sex unsettles a Baton Rouge lawyer, his wife, and her sister.
fields.Notes: Steven Soderbergh wrote it in eight days at 26; its Palme d'Or and box office started the independent boom of the 1990s and made Miramax.

fields.Title: Do the Right Thing
fields.Cast: Danny Aiello; Spike Lee; Ossie Davis; Giancarlo Esposito
fields.Clue: On the hottest day of the year in Bedford-Stuyvesant, a quarrel over whose photographs hang on a pizzeria wall ends in a riot.
fields.Notes: Radio Raheem is killed in a police chokehold; it closes with quotations from Martin Luther King Jr. and Malcolm X.

fields.Title: Pulp Fiction
fields.Cast: John Travolta; Samuel L. Jackson; Uma Thurman; Bruce Willis
fields.Clue: A hitman who quotes Ezekiel, a boxer who won't throw a fight, and a glowing briefcase share three stories told out of order.
fields.Notes: Its Palme d'Or, and $200 million taken on an $8 million budget, reshaped American cinema in the 1990s and rebuilt John Travolta's career.
fields.Still 2 caption: John Travolta and Samuel L. Jackson as Vincent and Jules

fields.Title: Three Colours: Red
fields.Cast: Irène Jacob; Jean-Louis Trintignant
fields.Clue: A Geneva model runs over a dog and finds its owner, a retired judge who eavesdrops on his neighbours' telephone calls.
fields.Notes: The last film Krzysztof Kieślowski completed; the trilogy follows the French flag and motto, and this one is fraternity.

fields.Title: The Shawshank Redemption
fields.Cast: Tim Robbins; Morgan Freeman
fields.Clue: A banker wrongly convicted of murder spends nineteen years tunnelling out of prison behind a pin-up poster.
fields.Notes: From a Stephen King novella; a box-office failure, it became through video the top-rated film on IMDb for over a decade.

fields.Title: Toy Story
fields.Cast: Tom Hanks; Tim Allen; Don Rickles
fields.Clue: A pull-string cowboy is displaced as a boy's favourite by a space ranger who does not know he is a toy.
fields.Notes: The first feature made entirely with computer animation; Randy Newman wrote the songs.

fields.Title: La Haine
fields.Cast: Vincent Cassel; Hubert Koundé; Saïd Taghmaoui
fields.Clue: Three friends, one Jewish, one Black, and one Arab, spend twenty-four hours in the Paris suburbs after a riot, one of them carrying a policeman's lost revolver.
fields.Notes: Shot in black and white; its story of a man falling from a building and repeating “So far so good” is the film's own summary of itself.

fields.Title: Fargo
fields.Cast: Frances McDormand; William H. Macy; Steve Buscemi
fields.Clue: A Minneapolis car salesman has his own wife kidnapped for the ransom, and a heavily pregnant police chief politely works it out.
fields.Notes: The opening claim that it is a true story is false; Frances McDormand won Best Actress, and there is a wood chipper.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Joel and Ethan Coen, 1996
fields.Still 2 caption: The Paul Bunyan statue made for the film by Rick Heinrichs

fields.Title: The Sweet Hereafter
fields.Cast: Ian Holm; Sarah Polley; Bruce Greenwood
fields.Clue: A lawyer arrives in a British Columbia town after a school bus crashes through the ice, hoping to organize a lawsuit.
fields.Notes: From Russell Banks's novel, and structured around “The Pied Piper of Hamelin,” which a surviving girl reads aloud.

fields.Title: Central Station
fields.Cast: Fernanda Montenegro; Vinícius de Oliveira
fields.Clue: A retired schoolteacher who writes letters for the illiterate at Rio's main railway terminus ends up escorting an orphaned boy across the northeast to find his father.
fields.Notes: Fernanda Montenegro was the first Brazilian nominated for a Best Actress Oscar; the boy was found shining shoes at the airport.

fields.Title: Festen
fields.Cast: Ulrich Thomsen; Henning Moritzen
fields.Clue: At a patriarch's sixtieth birthday party, his eldest son stands up to make a toast and accuses him of sexual abuse.
fields.Notes: Dogme 95's certificate number one, made under the “vow of chastity” Thomas Vinterberg and Lars von Trier had signed, and shot on a handheld consumer camcorder.

fields.Title: Ring
fields.Cast: Nanako Matsushima; Hiroyuki Sanada
fields.Clue: A journalist investigates a cursed videotape that kills its viewers seven days after they watch it.
fields.Notes: A drowned girl climbs out of a television set; it set off the J-horror wave and a Hollywood remake in 2002.

fields.Title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon
fields.Cast: Chow Yun-fat; Michelle Yeoh; Zhang Ziyi
fields.Clue: A warrior gives up his Green Destiny sword, a governor's daughter steals it, and they fight across the tops of a bamboo forest.
fields.Notes: Yuen Woo-ping choreographed the wire work; it took over $200 million worldwide and won the foreign-language Oscar.

fields.Title: Spirited Away
fields.Cast: Rumi Hiiragi; Miyu Irino
fields.Clue: A sulky ten-year-old whose parents have been turned into pigs is put to work in a bathhouse for spirits.
fields.Notes: The highest-grossing Japanese film for nearly two decades, and the only hand-drawn, non-English-language winner of the animation Oscar.

fields.Title: Amélie
fields.Cast: Audrey Tautou; Mathieu Kassovitz
fields.Clue: A shy Montmartre waitress finds a boy's box of treasures behind a bathroom tile, and takes to secretly arranging other people's happiness.
fields.Notes: Its Paris, all saturated green and gold, was criticized at home for being scrubbed of anything unpleasant; a garden gnome is sent travelling.

fields.Title: Lagaan
fields.Original title: Lagaan: Once Upon a Time in India
fields.Cast: Aamir Khan; Gracy Singh
fields.Clue: In 1893, a drought-stricken village accepts a British officer's wager: beat his men at cricket and pay no tax for three years.
fields.Notes: Nearly four hours long, with six songs and a final over that comes down to a no-ball; one of only three Indian films nominated for the foreign-language Oscar.

fields.Title: City of God
fields.Cast: Alexandre Rodrigues; Leandro Firmino
fields.Clue: A boy with a camera narrates twenty years of a Rio housing project's slide into a drug war, beginning with a chicken running from a knife.
fields.Notes: Most of the cast were untrained children from the favelas; it was nominated for four Oscars, though not for Best Foreign Language Film.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Fernando Meirelles and Kátia Lund, 2002

fields.Title: Oldboy
fields.Cast: Choi Min-sik; Yoo Ji-tae; Kang Hye-jung
fields.Clue: A man is imprisoned in a single room for fifteen years without being told why, and then given five days to find out.
fields.Notes: He eats a live octopus and fights down a corridor with a hammer in one unbroken shot; the middle film of Park Chan-wook's Vengeance Trilogy.

fields.Title: The Lives of Others
fields.Cast: Ulrich Mühe; Martina Gedeck; Sebastian Koch
fields.Clue: A Stasi captain bugs a playwright's flat in 1984 East Berlin, and quietly begins protecting him instead.
fields.Notes: Ulrich Mühe had himself been under Stasi surveillance; it won the foreign-language Oscar.

fields.Title: Pan's Labyrinth
fields.Cast: Ivana Baquero; Sergi López; Maribel Verdú
fields.Clue: In 1944 Spain, a girl whose mother has married a sadistic Falangist captain is told by a faun that she is a lost princess.
fields.Notes: One of her three tasks brings her to the Pale Man, who has eyes in his palms; it won three Oscars for its craft.

fields.Title: Slumdog Millionaire
fields.Cast: Dev Patel; Freida Pinto; Anil Kapoor
fields.Clue: A Mumbai tea boy one question from the top prize on a television quiz is arrested for cheating, and each answer turns out to come from his own life.
fields.Notes: A. R. Rahman scored it; it won eight Oscars, including Best Picture.

fields.Title: The Hurt Locker
fields.Cast: Jeremy Renner; Anthony Mackie
fields.Clue: A bomb-disposal sergeant in Iraq who has defused hundreds of devices cannot function at home, and goes back for another tour.
fields.Notes: Kathryn Bigelow became the first woman to win the directing Oscar, beating her ex-husband James Cameron's Avatar for Best Picture.

fields.Title: Man on Wire
fields.Cast: Philippe Petit; Annie Allix
fields.Clue: A documentary, structured like a heist film, about the Frenchman who in 1974 walked a cable strung between the World Trade Center towers.
fields.Notes: It never mentions the towers' destruction; it won the documentary Oscar.

fields.Title: The White Ribbon
fields.Cast: Christian Friedel; Burghart Klaußner
fields.Clue: In a north German village just before the First World War, a doctor's horse is tripped by a wire, and children are beaten and worse.
fields.Notes: Michael Haneke has said its children are the generation that would be adults under Nazism; shot in cold black and white, it won the Palme d'Or.

fields.Title: Once Upon a Time in Anatolia
fields.Cast: Muhammet Uzuner; Yılmaz Erdoğan
fields.Clue: Policemen, a prosecutor, a doctor, and a confessed killer drive around the steppe all night looking for a body the murderer cannot locate.
fields.Notes: Shared the Grand Prix at Cannes; the autopsy in the last act quietly changes the meaning of everything before it.

fields.Title: Gravity
fields.Cast: Sandra Bullock; George Clooney
fields.Clue: A medical engineer on her first shuttle mission is left tumbling through orbit after debris destroys her craft.
fields.Notes: It opens with an unbroken shot of about thirteen minutes, and most of it was shot inside an LED light box; it won seven Oscars, including Best Director.

fields.Title: Boyhood
fields.Cast: Ellar Coltrane; Patricia Arquette; Ethan Hawke
fields.Clue: A Texas boy and the actors around him were filmed a few days a year for twelve years, so that he grows from six to eighteen on screen.
fields.Notes: Shot on 35mm throughout so the twelve years would match; Patricia Arquette won Best Supporting Actress.

fields.Title: Raise the Red Lantern
fields.Cast: Gong Li; Ma Jingwu
fields.Clue: A university student becomes the fourth wife of a wealthy 1920s household, where the master's choice of wife for the night is announced outside her courtyard.
fields.Notes: The master's face is never clearly shown; China banned it while it was nominated for an Oscar.

fields.Title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
fields.Cast: Elijah Wood; Ian McKellen; Viggo Mortensen
fields.Clue: Nine companions set out from Rivendell to carry a small gold band toward a volcano, and a wizard falls with a Balrog at the bridge of Khazad-dûm.
fields.Notes: Peter Jackson shot all three parts at once in New Zealand; the trilogy won 17 Academy Awards in all.

fields.Title: The Great Train Robbery
fields.Cast: Broncho Billy Anderson; Justus D. Barnes
fields.Clue: Bandits hold up a telegraph office and a locomotive's passengers, and in the last shot an outlaw fires straight at the audience.
fields.Still caption: Justus D. Barnes fires at the audience in the final shot
fields.Notes: Twelve minutes that helped establish cross-cutting, often called the first Western; exhibitors could show the close-up at either end.

fields.Title: Dr. Mabuse the Gambler
fields.Cast: Rudolf Klein-Rogge; Aud Egede-Nissen
fields.Clue: A master of disguise and hypnosis manipulates the stock exchange and the card tables of inflation-era Berlin.
fields.Notes: Over four hours in two parts; Fritz Lang returned to the character twice, and the Nazis banned the 1933 sequel.

fields.Title: The Jazz Singer
fields.Cast: Al Jolson; May McAvoy; Warner Oland
fields.Clue: A cantor's son runs away to sing popular music, and returns to sing Kol Nidre in his dying father's place.
fields.Still caption: May McAvoy and Al Jolson, in blackface, before the dress rehearsal
fields.Notes: Mostly silent, with a few sung and spoken sequences on Vitaphone discs, it still ended the silent era; Al Jolson's blackface performance makes it hard to screen now.
fields.Still 2 caption: Jack Robin on stage in the final scene, in a publicity shot

fields.Title: Nosferatu
fields.Cast: Max Schreck; Greta Schröder
fields.Clue: An unlicensed version of Dracula brings a rat-toothed count to Wisborg on a plague ship, and sunlight destroys him.
fields.Still caption: Max Schreck as Count Orlok
fields.Notes: Bram Stoker's widow won a court order to destroy every print; the film survives because copies had already gone abroad.
fields.Still 2 caption: Count Orlok on the deck of the ship
fields.Still 3 caption: Orlok's shadow climbs the staircase

fields.Title: Un Chien Andalou
fields.Cast: Pierre Batcheff; Simone Mareuil
fields.Clue: A cloud crosses the moon as a razor slices an eye.
fields.Notes: Luis Buñuel and Salvador Dalí wrote it from their dreams; ants pour from a hole in a hand, and a man drags two pianos laden with dead donkeys.
fields.Still 2 caption: The hand caught in the door

fields.Title: Freaks
fields.Cast: Wallace Ford; Olga Baclanova; Harry Earles
fields.Clue: A trapeze artist marries a sideshow performer for his inheritance, and at the wedding banquet his friends chant that she is one of them.
fields.Still caption: Johnny Eck and Angelo Rossitto
fields.Notes: Tod Browning cast real sideshow performers; MGM cut a third of it, Britain banned it for thirty years, and it effectively ended his career.
fields.Still 2 caption: Among the circus performers

fields.Title: The Grapes of Wrath
fields.Cast: Henry Fonda; Jane Darwell; John Carradine
fields.Clue: An Oklahoma family driven off its land drives a loaded truck to California, and finds wage-cutting and a government camp.
fields.Still caption: Henry Fonda as Tom Joad
fields.Notes: Gregg Toland photographed it; Jane Darwell won Best Supporting Actress as Ma Joad, and John Steinbeck thought its ending improved on his.

fields.Title: The Maltese Falcon
fields.Cast: Humphrey Bogart; Mary Astor; Sydney Greenstreet; Peter Lorre
fields.Clue: A San Francisco private detective whose partner has been shot joins a hunt for a jewelled statuette that turns out to be lead.
fields.Notes: John Huston's first film as director, and the one that made Humphrey Bogart a leading man; it closes on “the stuff that dreams are made of.”
fields.Still 2 caption: Brigid O'Shaughnessy and Joel Cairo clash in front of the police

fields.Title: Sullivan's Travels
fields.Cast: Joel McCrea; Veronica Lake
fields.Clue: A director of profitable comedies sets out as a hobo to research a serious film, and learns on a chain gang that what prisoners want is a cartoon.
fields.Still caption: Veronica Lake and Joel McCrea
fields.Notes: The serious film he means to make is O Brother, Where Art Thou?, a title the Coen brothers took for their own film in 2000.

fields.Title: Double Indemnity
fields.Cast: Fred MacMurray; Barbara Stanwyck; Edward G. Robinson
fields.Clue: An insurance salesman and a client's wife murder her husband and stage it as a fall from a train, to collect twice the payout.
fields.Still caption: Fred MacMurray and Barbara Stanwyck as Walter Neff and Phyllis Dietrichson
fields.Notes: Raymond Chandler co-wrote it with Billy Wilder, and they detested each other; the confession is dictated into a Dictaphone.
fields.Still 2 caption: Phyllis and Walter meet at Jerry’s Market
fields.Still 3 caption: Phyllis hides behind Walter’s door

fields.Title: Meshes of the Afternoon
fields.Cast: Maya Deren; Alexander Hammid
fields.Clue: A woman follows a hooded figure with a mirror for a face into her own house again and again, until she multiplies into three versions of herself.
fields.Still caption: Maya Deren on the stairs
fields.Notes: Made for about $250, it is the founding work of the American avant-garde; Teiji Ito's score was added in 1959.

fields.Title: Brief Encounter
fields.Cast: Celia Johnson; Trevor Howard
fields.Clue: A married suburban woman and a married doctor meet by chance in a railway refreshment room, fall in love over a few Thursdays, and part.
fields.Still caption: Laura and Alec (Celia Johnson and Trevor Howard) part at the station
fields.Notes: From a Noël Coward play, set to Rachmaninoff; it was shot partly at Carnforth station in Lancashire, far from the bombing.

fields.Title: Murderers Among Us
fields.Cast: Hildegard Knef; Ernst Wilhelm Borchert
fields.Clue: A drink-ruined army surgeon in the rubble of Berlin sets out to shoot his former captain, now prospering by making saucepans from old helmets.
fields.Notes: The first German film made after the war, shot in the Soviet sector; the original ending, in which the killing happens, was changed.

fields.Title: The Red Shoes
fields.Cast: Moira Shearer; Anton Walbrook; Marius Goring
fields.Clue: A ballerina torn between an impresario who demands she dance and a composer who wants her to stop ends under a train in Monte Carlo.
fields.Still caption: Marius Goring as the composer Julian Craster
fields.Notes: Its seventeen-minute ballet takes over the film; Moira Shearer was a real ballerina, and Martin Scorsese funded its restoration.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger, 1948
fields.Still 2 caption: Moira Shearer in the Ballet of the Red Shoes

fields.Title: All About Eve
fields.Cast: Bette Davis; Anne Baxter; George Sanders
fields.Clue: An aging Broadway star takes on an adoring young fan as her assistant, and is systematically replaced by her.
fields.Still caption: Bette Davis in a publicity still
fields.Notes: The star tells her guests to fasten their seatbelts; its fourteen Oscar nominations were a record, since matched by Titanic and La La Land.
fields.Still 2 caption: George Sanders as Addison DeWitt
fields.Still 3 caption: Marilyn Monroe as Miss Casswell, with Anne Baxter, Bette Davis, and George Sanders

fields.Title: Los Olvidados
fields.Cast: Alfonso Mejía; Roberto Cobo
fields.Clue: Boys in the slums of Mexico City knock a legless beggar off his cart, and one dreams in slow motion of his mother offering him raw meat.
fields.Still caption: Alfonso Mejía (right, behind) as Pedro
fields.Notes: Pulled from Mexican cinemas after four days, it won Best Director at Cannes and returned; it is on UNESCO's Memory of the World register.
fields.Still 2 caption: Roberto Cobo as El Jaibo
fields.Still 3 caption: Mario Ramírez and Roberto Cobo (right)

fields.Title: The Big Heat
fields.Cast: Glenn Ford; Gloria Grahame; Lee Marvin
fields.Clue: A police sergeant whose wife is killed by a car bomb meant for him goes after the city's syndicate alone.
fields.Notes: A gangster's girlfriend has scalding coffee thrown in her face and returns the favour; the scene was cut in several countries.

fields.Title: La Strada
fields.Cast: Giulietta Masina; Anthony Quinn; Richard Basehart
fields.Clue: A brutish strongman buys a simple-minded girl from her mother to be his clown on the road, and abandons her when she breaks down.
fields.Still caption: Anthony Quinn and Giulietta Masina
fields.Notes: Giulietta Masina, Federico Fellini's wife, plays her to Nino Rota's theme; it won the first competitive Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film.
fields.Still 2 caption: Giulietta Masina as Gelsomina

fields.Title: Seven Samurai
fields.Cast: Toshiro Mifune; Takashi Shimura
fields.Clue: A village pays masterless swordsmen in rice to defend it from bandits at harvest.
fields.Notes: The final battle is fought in mud and rain, and the survivors are told the farmers have won, not them; remade as The Magnificent Seven.

fields.Title: Rififi
fields.Cast: Jean Servais; Carl Möhner; Jules Dassin
fields.Clue: Four men break into a Paris jeweller's through the ceiling in a half-hour heist with no dialogue and no music.
fields.Still caption: Tony tells the bound César, “I liked you, Macaroni”
fields.Notes: Jules Dassin, blacklisted out of Hollywood, made it in France and plays the safecracker under a pseudonym; several countries banned it as too instructive.

fields.Title: Invasion of the Body Snatchers
fields.Cast: Kevin McCarthy; Dana Wynter
fields.Clue: A small-town California doctor finds his patients' relatives being replaced by blank duplicates grown from pods.
fields.Notes: Read at the time as being about McCarthyism or about Communism, depending on the reader; the studio added a framing story that softens the ending.

fields.Title: Elevator to the Gallows
fields.Cast: Jeanne Moreau; Maurice Ronet
fields.Clue: A man who has murdered his lover's husband is trapped between floors of his office building overnight when the power is switched off.
fields.Notes: Louis Malle directed it at 25; Miles Davis improvised the score in one night, watching the film on a loop.

fields.Title: Touch of Evil
fields.Cast: Charlton Heston; Janet Leigh; Orson Welles; Marlene Dietrich
fields.Clue: A car bomb crosses the Mexican border in an unbroken opening crane shot of more than three minutes.
fields.Still caption: Orson Welles as Hank Quinlan
fields.Notes: Orson Welles plays the corrupt captain who plants evidence; a 1998 restoration followed his 58-page memo protesting the studio's recut.
fields.Still 2 caption: Janet Leigh and Charlton Heston
fields.Still 3 caption: Orson Welles, Victor Millan, Joseph Calleia, and Charlton Heston

fields.Title: Peeping Tom
fields.Cast: Carl Boehm; Moira Shearer; Anna Massey
fields.Clue: A focus puller kills women with a blade in his tripod leg while filming them watch their own deaths in a mirror.
fields.Still caption: Carl Boehm as Mark Lewis
fields.Notes: Released weeks before Psycho and savaged as obscene, it wrecked Michael Powell's career until Martin Scorsese led its rehabilitation.

fields.Title: Psycho
fields.Cast: Anthony Perkins; Janet Leigh; Vera Miles
fields.Clue: A secretary who has stolen $40,000 stops at a motel run by a nervous young man with a taxidermy hobby and a mother.
fields.Notes: She is killed forty minutes in, to Bernard Herrmann's strings; Hitchcock refused late admission to cinemas to protect the ending.
fields.Still 2 caption: Anthony Perkins and Janet Leigh as Norman Bates and Marion Crane
fields.Still 3 caption: The figure in the shower scene

fields.Title: The Innocents
fields.Cast: Deborah Kerr; Martin Stephens; Megs Jenkins
fields.Clue: A governess at a remote country house becomes convinced that her two charges are possessed by the spirits of a dead valet and her predecessor.
fields.Still caption: Deborah Kerr by candlelight; Freddie Francis darkened the edges of the frame
fields.Notes: From Henry James's The Turn of the Screw, with a script partly by Truman Capote; Freddie Francis darkened the edges of the frame.
fields.Still 2 caption: One of Jim Clark's layered dissolves

fields.Title: The Manchurian Candidate
fields.Cast: Frank Sinatra; Laurence Harvey; Angela Lansbury
fields.Clue: A brainwashed Korean War hero is triggered to kill by the queen of diamonds in a game of solitaire.
fields.Notes: A garden-club meeting dissolves into a Communist demonstration in Manchuria; Angela Lansbury, who plays his mother, was three years older than Laurence Harvey.

fields.Title: West Side Story
fields.Cast: Natalie Wood; Rita Moreno; George Chakiris
fields.Clue: Romeo and Juliet moves to 1950s Manhattan, with the Jets and the Sharks and a fire escape for a balcony.
fields.Still caption: Jose De Vega, Natalie Wood, and George Chakiris as Chino, Maria, and Bernardo
fields.Notes: Leonard Bernstein and Stephen Sondheim wrote the songs; it won ten Oscars, and Natalie Wood's singing is dubbed by Marni Nixon.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Robert Wise and Jerome Robbins, 1961
fields.Still 2 caption: The Jets attack Anita at Doc's drugstore

fields.Title: Jules and Jim
fields.Cast: Jeanne Moreau; Oskar Werner; Henri Serre
fields.Clue: An Austrian and a Frenchman love the same wilful woman before and after the First World War, until she drives off a broken bridge with one of them.
fields.Notes: From Henri-Pierre Roché's novel; Jeanne Moreau sings “Le Tourbillon,” about a whirlwind.

fields.Title: Dry Summer
fields.Cast: Erol Taş; Hülya Koçyiğit
fields.Clue: A landowner in an Aegean village dams the spring on his land and refuses water to everyone downstream.
fields.Notes: It won the Golden Bear in 1964, the first Turkish film to take a major festival prize, and was smuggled to Berlin against the government's wishes.

fields.Title: Jason and the Argonauts
fields.Cast: Todd Armstrong; Nancy Kovack; Honor Blackman
fields.Clue: Ray Harryhausen spent four and a half months animating its fight against seven sword-wielding skeletons.
fields.Still caption: Talos seizes the Argo
fields.Notes: The bronze giant Talos, harpies, and a hydra also appear; Bernard Herrmann wrote the score.
fields.Still 2 caption: Jason fights the Hydra
fields.Still 3 caption: Jason and his companions fight the skeletons

fields.Title: Onibaba
fields.Cast: Nobuko Otowa; Jitsuko Yoshimura
fields.Clue: Two women in a sea of tall grass kill stray samurai and sell their armour, until one puts on a demon mask she cannot get off.
fields.Notes: Kaneto Shindo said the mask was inspired by the keloid scars of atomic-bomb survivors; the grass was planted for the film.

fields.Title: I Am Cuba
fields.Cast: Sergio Corrieri; Salvador Wood
fields.Clue: A camera descends the side of a hotel into its swimming pool, and later floats out of a window above a funeral procession.
fields.Notes: Shot on infrared film that turns palms white and skies black; disowned by both countries, it was forgotten until Martin Scorsese and Francis Ford Coppola presented a restoration in 1995.

fields.Title: Persona
fields.Cast: Bibi Andersson; Liv Ullmann
fields.Clue: An actress stops speaking in the middle of a performance of Electra, and is sent to a seaside cottage with a talkative nurse.
fields.Notes: Partway through, the film seems to burn in the projector; later the two women's faces are printed over each other.
fields.Still 2 caption: Bibi Andersson and Liv Ullmann as Alma and Elisabet

fields.Title: The Graduate
fields.Cast: Dustin Hoffman; Anne Bancroft; Katharine Ross
fields.Clue: A young man home from college is given one word of advice, “plastics,” and is seduced by a family friend.
fields.Notes: Simon and Garfunkel's songs score it; Anne Bancroft was only six years older than Dustin Hoffman.

fields.Title: Belle de Jour
fields.Cast: Catherine Deneuve; Jean Sorel; Michel Piccoli
fields.Clue: A surgeon's wife secretly spends her afternoons working in a Paris brothel.
fields.Notes: A client's lacquered box is never opened, and Luis Buñuel refused to say what was in it; it won the Golden Lion.

fields.Title: Rosemary's Baby
fields.Cast: Mia Farrow; John Cassavetes; Ruth Gordon
fields.Clue: A young wife in a Gothic Manhattan apartment building is fed chocolate mousse with a chalky undertaste by her elderly neighbours.
fields.Still caption: Mia Farrow as Rosemary Woodhouse
fields.Notes: Shot at the Dakota; Ruth Gordon won Best Supporting Actress, and the child is never shown.

fields.Title: Salesman
fields.Cast: Paul Brennan; Charles McDevitt
fields.Clue: Four door-to-door Bible salesmen work Catholic neighbourhoods, and one of them, nicknamed the Badger, slowly stops being able to close.
fields.Notes: Albert and David Maysles and Charlotte Zwerin made it as direct cinema, with no narration and no interviews.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Albert and David Maysles, 1969

fields.Title: Midnight Cowboy
fields.Cast: Jon Voight; Dustin Hoffman
fields.Clue: A Texan dishwasher goes to New York to work as a gigolo, and teams up with a tubercular con man.
fields.Notes: The only X-rated film to win Best Picture; Dustin Hoffman's “I'm walkin' here!” was reportedly a reaction to a real taxi.

fields.Title: Once Upon a Time in the West
fields.Cast: Charles Bronson; Henry Fonda; Claudia Cardinale
fields.Clue: Three gunmen wait at a railway halt for a harmonica player, who kills them instead.
fields.Notes: Henry Fonda was cast against type as a man who shoots a child; Ennio Morricone's themes were written before shooting and played on set.

fields.Title: A Clockwork Orange
fields.Cast: Malcolm McDowell; Patrick Magee
fields.Clue: A gang leader who loves Beethoven is conditioned by the state with his eyelids clamped open.
fields.Still caption: Malcolm McDowell as Alex DeLarge
fields.Notes: From Anthony Burgess's novel; Stanley Kubrick withdrew it from British release in 1973, and it stayed unavailable there until after his death.

fields.Title: Harold and Maude
fields.Cast: Bud Cort; Ruth Gordon
fields.Clue: A rich young man who stages fake suicides and attends strangers' funerals falls in love with a 79-year-old woman.
fields.Notes: Cat Stevens wrote the songs; a flop on release, it became a repertory fixture.

fields.Title: Closely Watched Trains
fields.Cast: Václav Neckář; Josef Somr
fields.Clue: A shy apprentice at a sleepy station in occupied Czechoslovakia worries over his impotence, and ends up blowing up a German munitions transport.
fields.Notes: Jiří Menzel was 28 when it won the foreign-language Oscar in 1968; the Soviet invasion that August ended the Czech New Wave.

fields.Title: Kes
fields.Cast: David Bradley; Colin Welland; Brian Glover
fields.Clue: A bullied Barnsley schoolboy takes a young falcon from its nest and trains it.
fields.Notes: From Barry Hines's novel; distributors thought the Yorkshire accents unintelligible and nearly shelved it.

fields.Title: Land of Silence and Darkness
fields.Original title: Land des Schweigens und der Dunkelheit
fields.Cast: Fini Straubinger
fields.Clue: A woman deaf and blind since adolescence travels Bavaria visiting others like her, signing into their palms.
fields.Notes: Its opening image of ski jumpers is something Fini Straubinger said she remembered wanting to describe; Werner Herzog has admitted staging some moments.

fields.Title: Walkabout
fields.Cast: Jenny Agutter; David Gulpilil; Luc Roeg
fields.Clue: A girl and her small brother, abandoned in the outback by their father, survive with the help of an Aboriginal boy on his initiation journey.
fields.Notes: David Gulpilil's first film; Nicolas Roeg directed and shot it from a script of about fourteen pages.

fields.Title: The Harder They Come
fields.Cast: Jimmy Cliff; Carl Bradshaw; Janet Bartley
fields.Clue: A country boy comes to Kingston to cut a record, is cheated by the producer, and becomes an outlaw and folk hero with a hit on the charts.
fields.Notes: Jimmy Cliff stars; its soundtrack did more than any other record to take reggae international.

fields.Title: A Woman Under the Influence
fields.Cast: Gena Rowlands; Peter Falk
fields.Clue: A construction foreman's wife, whose behaviour embarrasses everyone around her, is committed for six months.
fields.Notes: John Cassavetes financed it himself; Gena Rowlands, his wife, plays her opposite Peter Falk.

fields.Title: Sholay
fields.Cast: Amitabh Bachchan; Dharmendra; Amjad Khan; Hema Malini
fields.Clue: A retired policeman whose arms were cut off hires two petty crooks to capture the bandit who massacred his family.
fields.Notes: The “curry Western” ran for five years at one Bombay cinema; a flop in its first fortnight, it became the highest-grossing Indian film for nineteen years.

fields.Title: Xala
fields.Cast: Thierno Leye; Seune Samb
fields.Clue: A businessman in newly independent Senegal takes a third wife, and finds himself impotent.
fields.Notes: To be cured he must let beggars spit on him; Ousmane Sembène, the father of African cinema, turned from novels to film to reach people who could not read.

fields.Title: Eraserhead
fields.Cast: Jack Nance; Charlotte Stewart
fields.Clue: A man with towering hair in an industrial wasteland is left to care for a swaddled, bleating, skinless infant.
fields.Notes: David Lynch shot it over five years, partly funded by a paper route; a woman in the radiator sings that in heaven everything is fine.

fields.Title: Dawn of the Dead
fields.Cast: David Emge; Ken Foree; Gaylen Ross
fields.Clue: Four survivors take a traffic helicopter to a Pennsylvania shopping mall, and seal themselves in among wandering zombies.
fields.Notes: George A. Romero's satire of consumerism; Tom Savini did the gore effects.
fields.Still 2 caption: The exploding-head effect in the tenement raid

fields.Title: Apocalypse Now
fields.Cast: Martin Sheen; Marlon Brando; Robert Duvall
fields.Clue: A captain is sent up a river into Cambodia to terminate a renegade colonel's command “with extreme prejudice.”
fields.Notes: A cavalry officer attacks a village to Wagner so his men can surf; the disastrous shoot is documented in Hearts of Darkness.

fields.Title: Days of Heaven
fields.Cast: Richard Gere; Brooke Adams; Sam Shepard; Linda Manz
fields.Clue: Migrant harvest workers pass off a couple as brother and sister so the woman can marry a dying Texas wheat farmer.
fields.Still caption: Shot at magic hour, around dawn and dusk
fields.Notes: Shot largely at magic hour; Néstor Almendros won the cinematography Oscar, and Terrence Malick did not make another film for twenty years.
fields.Still 2 caption: The locusts: peanut shells dropped from helicopters, run in reverse

fields.Title: Raging Bull
fields.Cast: Robert De Niro; Cathy Moriarty; Joe Pesci
fields.Clue: A Bronx middleweight's jealousy destroys his marriage and his brother along with his career, and he ends reciting a speech from On the Waterfront in a nightclub.
fields.Notes: Shot in black and white; Robert De Niro gained about sixty pounds for the later scenes, and Thelma Schoonmaker won her first Oscar for the editing.
fields.Still 2 caption: Robert De Niro as Jake LaMotta in the ring
fields.Still 3 caption: LaMotta in his leopard-print robe

fields.Title: The Shining
fields.Cast: Jack Nicholson; Shelley Duvall; Danny Lloyd
fields.Clue: A writer takes a winter caretaking job at an empty Colorado hotel, where his son rides a tricycle down the corridors toward twin girls.
fields.Notes: Stephen King disliked it; the manuscript turns out to be one sentence typed over and over, and Garrett Brown's early Steadicam follows the tricycle.
fields.Still 2 caption: “Here's Johnny!”

fields.Title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
fields.Cast: Henry Thomas; Drew Barrymore; Dee Wallace
fields.Clue: A suburban boy hides a stranded alien among his soft toys, and cycles him past a police roadblock into the sky.
fields.Notes: John Williams scored it; it was the highest-grossing film in the world for eleven years, and M&M's turned down the product placement that went to Reese's Pieces.

fields.Title: Scarface
fields.Cast: Al Pacino; Michelle Pfeiffer; Steven Bauer
fields.Clue: A Cuban refugee from the Mariel boatlift rises through Miami's cocaine trade, and dies in his mansion behind a mounted machine gun.
fields.Notes: Oliver Stone wrote it; mauled by critics in 1983, it later became a touchstone of hip hop.

fields.Title: Blood Simple
fields.Cast: Frances McDormand; John Getz; M. Emmet Walsh
fields.Clue: A Texas bar owner hires a sweaty private detective to kill his wife and her lover, and the detective double-crosses him.
fields.Notes: The Coen brothers' first film, its title from Dashiell Hammett's Red Harvest; Frances McDormand made her debut.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Joel and Ethan Coen, 1984

fields.Title: Come and See
fields.Cast: Aleksei Kravchenko; Olga Mironova
fields.Clue: A Belarusian boy digs up a rifle to join the partisans, and watches an SS unit burn a village's people inside a barn.
fields.Notes: His face ages visibly across the film, which ends running newsreel backward to Hitler as a baby; Elem Klimov never made another film.

fields.Title: Paris, Texas
fields.Cast: Harry Dean Stanton; Nastassja Kinski; Dean Stockwell
fields.Clue: A man walks out of the desert after four years of silence, reclaims his son, and finds his wife working behind one-way glass in a Houston peep show.
fields.Notes: Sam Shepard wrote it and Ry Cooder's slide guitar scores it; it won the Palme d'Or.

fields.Title: Brazil
fields.Cast: Jonathan Pryce; Robert De Niro; Katherine Helmond
fields.Clue: A dead fly in a printer causes the clerical error that sends the wrong man to be arrested, and a low-level functionary who dreams of flying is drawn into the machinery.
fields.Notes: Universal tried to impose a happy ending, and Terry Gilliam took out a trade advertisement asking the studio head when he would release it.

fields.Title: Down by Law
fields.Cast: Tom Waits; John Lurie; Roberto Benigni
fields.Clue: A disc jockey, a pimp, and a chattering Italian tourist share a New Orleans cell, and escape through the bayou.
fields.Notes: Shot in black and white by Robby Müller; Roberto Benigni learned his English lines phonetically.

fields.Title: Jesus of Montreal
fields.Cast: Lothaire Bluteau; Catherine Wilkening
fields.Clue: A young actor hired to modernize a shrine's Passion play finds his life repeating the story he is staging.
fields.Notes: The cleansing of the temple happens at an advertising audition; it won the Jury Prize at Cannes.

fields.Title: Hard Boiled
fields.Cast: Chow Yun-fat; Tony Leung
fields.Clue: A clarinet-playing Hong Kong policeman shoots his way through a hospital in a take of nearly three minutes, while babies are carried out of the maternity ward.
fields.Notes: John Woo's last Hong Kong film before Hollywood; the “single take” hides several joins.

fields.Title: Reservoir Dogs
fields.Cast: Harvey Keitel; Tim Roth; Michael Madsen; Steve Buscemi
fields.Clue: Six criminals given colour-coded aliases argue about Madonna and tipping, and regroup in a warehouse after a diamond robbery that is never shown.
fields.Still caption: The criminals' slow-motion walk in the opening
fields.Notes: Quentin Tarantino's first film, much of its budget from Harvey Keitel; the ear-cutting scene, set to “Stuck in the Middle with You,” caused walkouts at Sundance.

fields.Title: Naked
fields.Cast: David Thewlis; Lesley Sharp; Katrin Cartlidge
fields.Clue: A brilliant, vicious Mancunian talks his way across night-time London, delivering apocalyptic lectures to anyone who will listen.
fields.Notes: Mike Leigh built it from months of improvisation; David Thewlis won Best Actor at Cannes, and Leigh Best Director.

fields.Title: Short Cuts
fields.Cast: Andie MacDowell; Tim Robbins; Julianne Moore; Jack Lemmon
fields.Clue: Twenty-two Los Angeles characters cross paths during a medfly spraying campaign, from fishermen who don't report a body to a phone-sex worker changing diapers.
fields.Notes: From nine Raymond Carver stories and a poem, moved to Los Angeles; the whole cast shared a special award at Venice.

fields.Title: Heavenly Creatures
fields.Cast: Melanie Lynskey; Kate Winslet
fields.Clue: Two Christchurch schoolgirls build an imaginary kingdom, and when their families try to separate them they kill one of the mothers.
fields.Notes: A true story, and Kate Winslet's first film; one of the real girls later became the crime novelist Anne Perry.

fields.Title: Drifting Clouds
fields.Cast: Kati Outinen; Kari Väänänen
fields.Clue: A tram driver and a restaurant head waiter both lose their jobs in the Finnish recession, and sink through debt and humiliation in perfect deadpan.
fields.Notes: The first of Aki Kaurismäki's Finland trilogy; his usual lead, Matti Pellonpää, died before shooting and is honoured in a photograph.

fields.Title: Breaking the Waves
fields.Cast: Emily Watson; Stellan Skarsgård
fields.Clue: A devout young woman on a Scottish island marries an oil-rig worker who, paralyzed, asks her to take lovers and describe them to him.
fields.Notes: Emily Watson's debut; bells ring over the sea at the end, and the handheld image was degraded through video on purpose.

fields.Title: Taste of Cherry
fields.Cast: Homayoun Ershadi; Abdolrahman Bagheri
fields.Clue: A man drives around the hills outside Tehran looking for someone willing to bury him after he kills himself.
fields.Still caption: Homayoun Ershadi as Mr. Badii
fields.Notes: It shared the Palme d'Or in 1997, and ends on video footage of the crew; a taxidermist talks him through mulberries.

fields.Title: Werckmeister Harmonies
fields.Cast: Lars Rudolph; Peter Fitz; Hanna Schygulla
fields.Clue: A circus brings a stuffed whale to a freezing Hungarian town, and a mob forms and wrecks a hospital.
fields.Notes: About 39 shots in 145 minutes, opening with a drunk demonstrating an eclipse in a bar; adapted from László Krasznahorkai's novel.

fields.Title: Amores Perros
fields.Cast: Gael García Bernal; Emilio Echevarría
fields.Clue: A car crash in Mexico City connects a boy who enters his brother's dog in illegal fights, a model with a lapdog, and a homeless hitman surrounded by strays.
fields.Notes: Alejandro González Iñárritu's first feature, and the first of his Death Trilogy with the writer Guillermo Arriaga.

fields.Title: In the Mood for Love
fields.Cast: Maggie Cheung; Tony Leung
