fields.Clue: Two neighbours in 1962 Hong Kong discover that their spouses are having an affair with each other, and rehearse the confrontation themselves.
fields.Notes: They pass on the stairs to the noodle stall in slow motion to a waltz; the secret is finally whispered into a hole at Angkor Wat.

fields.Title: Mulholland Drive
fields.Cast: Naomi Watts; Laura Harring; Justin Theroux
fields.Clue: An amnesiac car-crash survivor and an aspiring actress find a blue box and a blue key, and then everyone changes identity.
fields.Still caption: Betty (Naomi Watts) arrives in Los Angeles, with Irene (Jeanne Bates)
fields.Notes: At the Club Silencio a singer collapses while her voice goes on; the film began as a rejected television pilot.
fields.Still 2 caption: Betty and Rita at Club Silencio
fields.Still 3 caption: Naomi Watts and Laura Harring as Betty and Rita

fields.Title: Good Bye, Lenin!
fields.Cast: Daniel Brühl; Katrin Sass
fields.Clue: A committed East German socialist wakes from a coma after the Wall has fallen, and her son recreates the vanished country in her bedroom.
fields.Notes: The biggest German hit of its year, it popularized the word Ostalgie; Yann Tiersen wrote the score.

fields.Title: Tsotsi
fields.Cast: Presley Chweneyagae; Terry Pheto
fields.Clue: A Soweto gang leader shoots a woman for her car, and finds her baby on the back seat.
fields.Notes: From Athol Fugard's 1960s novel, moved to the post-apartheid present; it won the foreign-language Oscar.

fields.Title: Caché
fields.Cast: Daniel Auteuil; Juliette Binoche
fields.Clue: A Paris television presenter receives videotapes of his own front door, wrapped in childish drawings of a figure bleeding from the mouth.
fields.Notes: The guilt they uncover goes back to an Algerian boy and the massacre of 17 October 1961; Michael Haneke has never said who sends the tapes.

fields.Title: Times and Winds
fields.Cast: Özkan Ozen; Ali Bıçer; Elit İşcan
fields.Clue: Three children in a mountain village live through the five daily calls to prayer that divide the film.
fields.Notes: The Turkish title means “five times,” the prayer times; Reha Erdem set it to Arvo Pärt.

fields.Title: Ten Canoes
fields.Director: Rolf de Heer and Peter Djigirr
fields.Cast: Jamie Gulpilil; Crusoe Kurddal
fields.Clue: The first feature made entirely in an Australian Aboriginal language, in which a goose-egg hunt frames an older story about a man who covets his brother's wife.
fields.Notes: Narrated in English by David Gulpilil, and built around Donald Thomson's 1930s photographs of the same swamp.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Rolf de Heer and Peter Djigirr, 2006

fields.Title: There Will Be Blood
fields.Cast: Daniel Day-Lewis; Paul Dano
fields.Clue: A silver prospector turned oilman builds a California empire, and settles his score with a young preacher in a private bowling alley.
fields.Notes: Loosely from Upton Sinclair's Oil!, to Jonny Greenwood's score; its first fifteen minutes have no dialogue.

fields.Title: The Secret in Their Eyes
fields.Cast: Ricardo Darín; Soledad Villamil
fields.Clue: A retired court investigator writing a novel reopens a 1974 rape and murder, whose suspect was found through his gaze in old photographs.
fields.Notes: It won the foreign-language Oscar; its chase through a packed football stadium is a composite made to look like one shot.

fields.Title: The Kid with a Bike
fields.Cast: Thomas Doret; Cécile de France
fields.Clue: An eleven-year-old in a children's home refuses to believe his father has abandoned him, and is taken in on weekends by a hairdresser.
fields.Notes: Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne's first use of music, four short bursts of Beethoven; it shared the Grand Prix at Cannes.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne, 2011

fields.Title: Holy Motors
fields.Cast: Denis Lavant; Édith Scob; Kylie Minogue
fields.Clue: A man is driven around Paris in a white stretch limousine to nine appointments, at each of which he becomes someone else.
fields.Notes: In one he is a sewer creature who eats flowers and abducts a model; the limousines talk to each other in the garage at the end.

fields.Title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
fields.Cast: Ralph Fiennes; Tony Revolori; Saoirse Ronan
fields.Clue: A concierge in a fictional interwar republic inherits a painting of a boy with an apple, is framed for murder, and is chased over the Alps on a sled.
fields.Notes: Its nested time periods are shot in three aspect ratios; it won four Oscars for its craft, and credits Stefan Zweig as its inspiration.
fields.Still 2 caption: The miniature hotel built for the film

fields.Title: Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker's Apocalypse
fields.Cast: Francis Ford Coppola; Eleanor Coppola
fields.Clue: A documentary built from the audio a director's wife secretly recorded during his disastrous shoot in the Philippines.
fields.Notes: Eleanor Coppola's tapes record a typhoon, Martin Sheen's heart attack, and Francis Ford Coppola admitting he has no ending.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Fax Bahr and George Hickenlooper, 1991

fields.Title: The General
fields.Cast: Buster Keaton; Marion Mack
fields.Clue: A Confederate railway engineer rejected by the army chases his stolen locomotive north and back again, never once changing expression.
fields.Still caption: Buster Keaton riding the cowcatcher
fields.Notes: Based on the Andrews Raid of 1862; a real bridge collapses under a real train, and the film's failure ended Buster Keaton's independence.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Buster Keaton and Clyde Bruckman, 1926
fields.Still 2 caption: Buster Keaton with the Union mortar

fields.Title: Modern Times
fields.Cast: Charlie Chaplin; Paulette Goddard
fields.Clue: A factory worker is fed by a malfunctioning automatic lunch machine, and tightens bolts until he is swallowed by the gears.
fields.Still caption: The Tramp in the machine
fields.Notes: The Tramp's last appearance, and the only film in which his voice is heard, singing nonsense Italian; Chaplin was still refusing dialogue in 1936.

fields.Title: Bringing Up Baby
fields.Cast: Cary Grant; Katharine Hepburn
fields.Clue: A paleontologist loses a prized bone to a dog, and is dragged around Connecticut by an heiress with a tame leopard.
fields.Still caption: Katharine Hepburn as Susan Vance
fields.Notes: A flop that got Katharine Hepburn labelled box-office poison; it is now the standard example of screwball comedy.
fields.Still 2 caption: Katharine Hepburn and Cary Grant
fields.Still 3 caption: Katharine Hepburn and the leopard Nissa in a publicity photograph

fields.Title: Ugetsu
fields.Cast: Masayuki Mori; Machiko Kyō
fields.Clue: In the sixteenth-century civil wars, a potter chasing profit is seduced by a noblewoman who turns out to be a ghost.
fields.Notes: A boat glides out of the mist across Lake Biwa; it took the Silver Lion at Venice and, with Rashomon, opened Japanese cinema to the West.

fields.Title: Rear Window
fields.Cast: James Stewart; Grace Kelly; Thelma Ritter
fields.Clue: A photographer laid up with a broken leg watches his courtyard neighbours through a telephoto lens, and becomes convinced one has murdered his wife.
fields.Still caption: Grace Kelly as Lisa Fremont
fields.Notes: The whole film stays inside one apartment, looking out on a courtyard of 31 apartments built on a Paramount stage.
fields.Still 2 caption: James Stewart as L. B. Jefferies
fields.Still 3 caption: Jefferies, in his wheelchair, with Lisa

fields.Title: Wild Strawberries
fields.Cast: Victor Sjöström; Ingrid Thulin; Bibi Andersson
fields.Clue: An old professor driving to Lund for an honorary degree dreams of a clock without hands and of his own coffin.
fields.Notes: Victor Sjöström, the silent director of The Phantom Carriage, plays him at 78.
fields.Still 2 caption: Ingmar Bergman (left) and Victor Sjöström during filming in Solna

fields.Title: North by Northwest
fields.Cast: Cary Grant; Eva Marie Saint; James Mason
fields.Clue: An advertising man mistaken for a spy who does not exist is attacked by a crop duster on an empty country road.
fields.Still caption: Cary Grant in a still from the film
fields.Notes: It ends on Mount Rushmore; Bernard Herrmann wrote the fandango, and Saul Bass designed the titles.
fields.Still 2 caption: James Mason, Eva Marie Saint, and Cary Grant at Mount Rushmore during filming

fields.Title: Cléo from 5 to 7
fields.Cast: Corinne Marchand; Antoine Bourseiller
fields.Clue: A pop singer waits ninety minutes, in near real time, for the result of a biopsy.
fields.Notes: Chapter titles keep the clock; she finally meets a soldier on leave from Algeria in the Parc Montsouris.

fields.Title: Lawrence of Arabia
fields.Cast: Peter O'Toole; Omar Sharif; Alec Guinness
fields.Clue: A misfit British officer crosses the Nefud Desert to take Aqaba from the landward side.
fields.Still caption: Peter O'Toole as T. E. Lawrence
fields.Notes: A match blown out cuts to a desert sunrise; shot in 70mm, it has no women in speaking parts, and Maurice Jarre wrote the score in six weeks.

fields.Title: 8½
fields.Cast: Marcello Mastroianni; Anouk Aimée; Claudia Cardinale
fields.Clue: A film director with nothing to say hides at a spa from his producer, his wife, and his mistress.
fields.Still caption: Marcello Mastroianni as Guido Anselmi
fields.Notes: It ends with everyone in his life joining a circus parade; the title counts Federico Fellini's previous films, and it inspired the musical Nine.
fields.Still 2 caption: Marcello Mastroianni as Guido Anselmi

fields.Title: Daisies
fields.Cast: Ivana Karbanová; Jitka Cerhová
fields.Clue: Two young women decide that since the world is spoiled they will be spoiled too, and wreck a banquet laid for officials.
fields.Notes: Banned at home for its food-wasting, not its politics; Věra Chytilová was forbidden to work for years afterward.

fields.Title: The Conformist
fields.Cast: Jean-Louis Trintignant; Stefania Sandrelli; Dominique Sanda
fields.Clue: A man who wants above all to be normal joins Mussolini's secret police, and is sent to Paris to have his old professor killed.
fields.Notes: Vittorio Storaro's photography slices light through Fascist architecture; Francis Ford Coppola and Martin Scorsese both cite it.

fields.Title: Solaris
fields.Cast: Donatas Banionis; Natalya Bondarchuk
fields.Clue: A psychologist sent to a station orbiting a sentient ocean finds the crew haunted by physical copies of people from their memories, including his dead wife.
fields.Notes: From Stanisław Lem, who disliked it; a five-minute drive on a Tokyo expressway stands in for the city of the future.

fields.Title: Barry Lyndon
fields.Cast: Ryan O'Neal; Marisa Berenson; Patrick Magee
fields.Clue: An Irish adventurer duels, deserts from two armies, cheats at cards across Europe, and marries a countess.
fields.Notes: From Thackeray; its interiors are lit by candles alone, shot with f/0.7 lenses made for NASA.

fields.Title: Nashville
fields.Cast: Lily Tomlin; Ronee Blakley; Keith Carradine; Henry Gibson
fields.Clue: Twenty-four characters converge on a country-music city during a populist presidential campaign whose candidate is heard only from a loudspeaker van.
fields.Notes: It ends with a shooting at a rally and the crowd singing “It Don't Worry Me”; the cast wrote their own songs, and Keith Carradine's “I'm Easy” won the Oscar.

fields.Title: Goodfellas
fields.Cast: Ray Liotta; Robert De Niro; Joe Pesci; Lorraine Bracco
fields.Clue: A half-Irish boy from Brooklyn rises through a crew, narrating from his first line: as far back as he can remember, he always wanted to be a gangster.
fields.Notes: A Steadicam takes a date in through the kitchen of the Copacabana; Joe Pesci won Best Supporting Actor for a “funny how?” scene he drew from life.

fields.Title: Schindler's List
fields.Cast: Liam Neeson; Ralph Fiennes; Ben Kingsley
fields.Clue: A Sudeten German profiteer staffs his enamelware factory with Jewish workers, and ends up spending his fortune to save them.
fields.Notes: The black and white is broken once by a small girl's red coat; Steven Spielberg took no salary and founded the Shoah Foundation with the profits.

fields.Title: Beau Travail
fields.Cast: Denis Lavant; Michel Subor; Grégoire Colin
fields.Clue: A Foreign Legion sergeant in Djibouti is consumed by jealousy of a new recruit.
fields.Notes: Loosely from Billy Budd; it ends with the sergeant dancing alone to “The Rhythm of the Night.”

fields.Title: Yi Yi
fields.Cast: Wu Nien-jen; Kelly Lee; Jonathan Chang
fields.Clue: A Taipei family's year runs from a wedding to a funeral, while the eight-year-old son photographs the backs of people's heads because they cannot see them.
fields.Notes: It won Best Director at Cannes but was not released in Taiwan in Edward Yang's lifetime.

fields.Title: Persepolis
fields.Cast: Chiara Mastroianni; Catherine Deneuve
fields.Clue: A girl grows up through the Iranian revolution and the war with Iraq, in stark hand-drawn black and white.
fields.Notes: Marjane Satrapi adapted her own graphic novel; Iran protested its selection at Cannes, where it shared the Jury Prize.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Marjane Satrapi and Vincent Paronnaud, 2007

fields.Title: Grave of the Fireflies
fields.Cast: Tsutomu Tatsumi; Ayano Shiraishi
fields.Clue: A teenage boy and his small sister, orphaned by the firebombing of Kobe, live in a hillside shelter until she dies of malnutrition.
fields.Notes: Isao Takahata made it for Studio Ghibli, and it was released on a double bill with My Neighbor Totoro.

fields.Title: Andrei Rublev
fields.Cast: Anatoly Solonitsyn; Ivan Lapikov
fields.Clue: A fifteenth-century icon painter takes a vow of silence after killing a man in a Tatar raid, and a boy casts an enormous bell.
fields.Notes: It opens with a peasant's hot-air balloon flight and ends in colour on the finished icons; the Soviet authorities shelved it for five years.

fields.Title: Mad Max: Fury Road
fields.Cast: Tom Hardy; Charlize Theron; Nicholas Hoult
fields.Clue: An imperator drives a war rig off its fuel run to smuggle five wives away from a warlord who rations water.
fields.Notes: Almost the whole film is one chase out and back, with a flame-throwing guitarist on a truck of drummers; it won six Oscars, all for craft.

fields.Title: Son of Saul
fields.Cast: Géza Röhrig; Levente Molnár
fields.Clue: A Sonderkommando prisoner at Auschwitz tries to find a rabbi to bury a boy he takes for his son.
fields.Notes: The camera stays on his face in a shallow-focus, near-square frame while the horror happens out of focus; it won the foreign-language Oscar.

fields.Title: Carol
fields.Cast: Cate Blanchett; Rooney Mara
fields.Clue: A Manhattan shopgirl in 1952 sells a train set to an elegant customer who leaves her gloves behind on purpose.
fields.Notes: From Patricia Highsmith's The Price of Salt, published under a pseudonym because it did not punish its lovers; shot on 16mm.

fields.Title: The Assassin
fields.Cast: Shu Qi; Chang Chen
fields.Clue: A ninth-century killer trained by a nun is ordered to murder the cousin she was once betrothed to, and does not.
fields.Notes: The fights last seconds and the takes last minutes; Hou Hsiao-hsien won Best Director at Cannes.

fields.Title: Moonlight
fields.Cast: Trevante Rhodes; Mahershala Ali; Naomie Harris
fields.Clue: Three chapters in the life of a boy growing up poor, Black, and gay in Miami, each with a different actor and a different name.
fields.Notes: A drug dealer teaches him to swim; it won Best Picture after the envelope was misread on stage.

fields.Title: Toni Erdmann
fields.Cast: Peter Simonischek; Sandra Hüller
fields.Clue: A retired music teacher with joke false teeth turns up in Bucharest to pester his management-consultant daughter, disguised as a life coach.
fields.Notes: Its Whitney Houston singalong is the heart of the film; it was the Cannes critics' clear favourite, and won nothing there.

fields.Title: Arrival
fields.Cast: Amy Adams; Jeremy Renner; Forest Whitaker
fields.Clue: A linguist is brought in to learn the written language of aliens, circular ink marks with no direction in time.
fields.Notes: From Ted Chiang's “Story of Your Life”; Max Richter's “On the Nature of Daylight” bookends it.

fields.Title: Get Out
fields.Cast: Daniel Kaluuya; Allison Williams; Catherine Keener
fields.Clue: A Black photographer visiting his white girlfriend's family is hypnotized with a teaspoon and a teacup into a paralyzed “sunken place.”
fields.Notes: Made for about $4.5 million, it took over $250 million; Jordan Peele won the screenplay Oscar.

fields.Title: Call Me by Your Name
fields.Cast: Timothée Chalamet; Armie Hammer; Michael Stuhlbarg
fields.Clue: A seventeen-year-old and his father's American graduate student circle each other through a summer in northern Italy.
fields.Notes: The father's speech about not killing feeling is its centre; James Ivory won the adapted-screenplay Oscar at 89.

fields.Title: Lady Bird
fields.Cast: Saoirse Ronan; Laurie Metcalf; Tracy Letts
fields.Clue: A Sacramento Catholic-school senior who insists on a name she gave herself throws herself out of a moving car during an argument with her mother.
fields.Notes: Gerwig was only the fifth woman nominated for the directing Oscar; the film is set in 2002–03 and is semi-autobiographical.

fields.Title: Phantom Thread
fields.Cast: Daniel Day-Lewis; Vicky Krieps; Lesley Manville
fields.Clue: A fastidious 1950s London couturier takes a waitress as his muse, and she learns to poison him with mushrooms.
fields.Notes: Paul Thomas Anderson shot it himself, to Jonny Greenwood's score; it was announced as Daniel Day-Lewis's last film.

fields.Title: Shoplifters
fields.Cast: Lily Franky; Sakura Ando; Kirin Kiki
fields.Clue: A makeshift Tokyo household living off a grandmother's pension and petty theft takes in a neglected little girl.
fields.Notes: It won the Palme d'Or; Kore-eda has said it grew out of news reports of families concealing deaths to keep drawing pensions.

fields.Title: Roma
fields.Cast: Yalitza Aparicio; Marina de Tavira
fields.Clue: A live-in housekeeper for a middle-class family in 1970s Mexico City loses her baby during the Corpus Christi massacre.
fields.Notes: Shot in black and white, largely in slow lateral pans; Alfonso Cuarón wrote, shot, and edited it, and it was the first Netflix film nominated for Best Picture.

fields.Title: Burning
fields.Cast: Yoo Ah-in; Steven Yeun; Jeon Jong-seo
fields.Clue: A would-be writer meets a woman who mimes peeling a tangerine, and her rich friend, who says he burns down a greenhouse every two months.
fields.Notes: From Haruki Murakami's “Barn Burning,” which takes its title from William Faulkner; it topped Screen's Cannes critics' grid and won nothing.

fields.Title: Parasite
fields.Cast: Song Kang-ho; Cho Yeo-jeong; Lee Sun-kyun
fields.Clue: A poor family living in a semi-basement cons its way, one member at a time, into jobs with a rich family.
fields.Notes: The first non-English-language film to win Best Picture, and the first since 1955 to take both that and the Palme d'Or.
fields.Still 2 caption: The house, built on a set; everything above the ground floor was added digitally

fields.Title: Nomadland
fields.Cast: Frances McDormand; David Strathairn
fields.Clue: A widow whose Nevada company town loses its ZIP code converts a van and follows seasonal work around the West, among real nomads playing themselves.
fields.Notes: Chloé Zhao became the second woman, and the first woman of colour, to win the directing Oscar.

fields.Title: The Power of the Dog
fields.Cast: Benedict Cumberbatch; Kirsten Dunst; Kodi Smit-McPhee
fields.Clue: A Montana rancher who castrates calves bare-handed torments his brother's new wife, until her delicate son befriends him.
fields.Notes: The title comes from Psalm 22; Jane Campion became the first woman nominated twice for the directing Oscar, and won.

fields.Title: Tár
fields.Cast: Cate Blanchett; Nina Hoss; Noémie Merlant
fields.Clue: A celebrated conductor preparing Mahler's Fifth in Berlin humiliates a student in a Juilliard masterclass, and is undone by the suicide of a former protégée.
fields.Notes: Cate Blanchett learned to conduct, play piano, and speak German for it; it ends with her conducting a video-game score in Southeast Asia.

fields.Title: Oppenheimer
fields.Cast: Cillian Murphy; Robert Downey Jr.; Emily Blunt
fields.Clue: A physicist's security-clearance hearing and a cabinet nominee's confirmation are cross-cut, in colour and in black and white, around the Trinity test.
fields.Notes: Christopher Nolan shot it on IMAX film; it won seven Oscars, including Best Picture, and its joint release with Barbie became a cultural event.

fields.Title: Anatomy of a Fall
fields.Cast: Sandra Hüller; Swann Arlaud; Milo Machado-Graner
fields.Clue: A German writer is tried in Grenoble for her husband's fatal plunge from their chalet window, with their partially sighted son as a witness.
fields.Notes: It won the Palme d'Or and the screenplay Oscar; the dog, Messi, won the Palm Dog.

fields.Title: The Zone of Interest
fields.Cast: Christian Friedel; Sandra Hüller
fields.Clue: The Auschwitz commandant and his wife tend their garden on the other side of the camp wall, while the atrocity exists only in the sound.
fields.Notes: Jonathan Glazer used fixed cameras running unmanned through the house; it won the international-feature and sound Oscars.

fields.Title: Poor Things
fields.Cast: Emma Stone; Willem Dafoe; Mark Ruffalo
fields.Clue: A surgeon revives a drowned woman with her own unborn baby's brain, and she learns the world at speed in Lisbon, on a cruise ship, and in a Paris brothel.
fields.Notes: From Alasdair Gray's novel; it won four Oscars, including Best Actress for Emma Stone.

fields.Title: Everything Everywhere All at Once
fields.Cast: Michelle Yeoh; Ke Huy Quan; Jamie Lee Curtis
fields.Clue: A laundromat owner in the middle of a tax audit borrows skills from her selves in other universes, including one where everyone has hot dogs for fingers.
fields.Notes: It won seven Oscars, including Best Picture; the villain's weapon is a bagel with everything on it.
fields.Poster caption: Release poster · Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert, 2022

fields.Title: Past Lives
fields.Cast: Greta Lee; Teo Yoo; John Magaro
fields.Clue: Two childhood friends separated when one family emigrates from Seoul reconnect twice across twenty-four years, the second time in New York, where she is married.
fields.Notes: The Korean idea of in-yun, ties accumulated across past lives, is its argument; it was nominated for Best Picture.

fields.Title: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
fields.Original title: Portrait de la jeune fille en feu
fields.Cast: Noémie Merlant; Adèle Haenel
fields.Clue: A painter is sent to a Breton island in the 1770s to paint a woman in secret for her betrothal, memorizing her face on their walks.
fields.Notes: It ends on a face across a concert hall during Vivaldi's “Summer”; it won the screenplay prize at Cannes.

fields.Title: Drive My Car
fields.Cast: Hidetoshi Nishijima; Tōko Miura
fields.Clue: A stage director rehearsing Uncle Vanya in several languages at once is assigned a young woman as chauffeur for his red Saab.
fields.Notes: From a Haruki Murakami story; the opening credits arrive forty minutes in, and it won the international-feature Oscar.

fields.Title: Stanley Kubrick
fields.Clue: A Bronx-born perfectionist who moved to England and made thirteen features in forty-six years, each researched to exhaustion and shot in endless takes.
fields.Works: Dr. Strangelove; 2001: A Space Odyssey; A Clockwork Orange; Barry Lyndon; The Shining
fields.Notes: He began as a staff photographer for Look magazine at seventeen; Eyes Wide Shut was finished days before his death.

fields.Title: Fritz Lang
fields.Clue: A Viennese-born master of Weimar cinema who left Germany in 1933 and made hard, fatalistic thrillers in Hollywood for twenty years.
fields.Works: Dr. Mabuse the Gambler; Metropolis; M; The Big Heat
fields.Notes: He claimed Goebbels offered him charge of German film and that he fled the same night, a story he later admitted embellishing.

fields.Title: Alfred Hitchcock
fields.Clue: The English-born “master of suspense,” who appeared briefly in almost all of his own films and coined the term MacGuffin.
fields.Works: Rear Window; Vertigo; North by Northwest; Psycho
fields.Notes: He moved to Hollywood in 1939 on a Selznick contract, and never won a competitive directing Oscar.

fields.Title: Luis Buñuel
fields.Clue: An Aragonese Surrealist who made his first film with Salvador Dalí, spent two decades working in Mexico, and ended with elegant French satires of the bourgeoisie.
fields.Works: Un Chien Andalou; Los Olvidados; Belle de Jour; The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie
fields.Notes: During the Civil War he worked for the Republic in Paris, and afterward for the MoMA in New York.

fields.Title: Michael Powell
fields.Clue: The director half of the British partnership that signed its films “The Archers,” sharing one credit with a Hungarian émigré screenwriter.
fields.Works: A Matter of Life and Death; The Red Shoes; Peeping Tom
fields.Notes: His partner, Emeric Pressburger, wrote the scripts; Peeping Tom wrecked his career, and Thelma Schoonmaker, Martin Scorsese's editor, became his wife.

fields.Title: Billy Wilder
fields.Clue: A Viennese-born, Berlin-trained screenwriter who fled in 1933 and became Hollywood's sharpest cynic.
fields.Works: Double Indemnity; Sunset Boulevard; Some Like It Hot
fields.Notes: He wrote with Charles Brackett and then I. A. L. Diamond; he won six Oscars and collected modern art with the proceeds.

fields.Title: Ingmar Bergman
fields.Clue: A Swedish pastor's son who made about sixty films of faith, silence, and marriage, many of them on the island of Fårö with the cinematographer Sven Nykvist.
fields.Works: The Seventh Seal; Wild Strawberries; Persona
fields.Notes: He ran Sweden's Royal Dramatic Theatre and left the country for years after a tax prosecution in 1976.

fields.Title: Federico Fellini
fields.Clue: A cartoonist from Rimini who began in neorealism and ended in circus, and gave the world its word for celebrity photographers.
fields.Works: La Strada; La Dolce Vita; 8½
fields.Notes: He won four foreign-language Oscars and an honorary one; Giulietta Masina, his wife, starred in several of his films.

fields.Title: Steven Spielberg
fields.Clue: The most commercially successful director in history, who invented the summer blockbuster with a malfunctioning mechanical shark.
fields.Works: Jaws; E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial; Schindler's List
fields.Notes: He co-founded DreamWorks in 1994; the Shoah Foundation was paid for out of one film's profits.

fields.Title: Martin Scorsese
fields.Clue: A Little Italy asthmatic who nearly became a priest, and turned Catholic guilt into American crime cinema, nine times with Robert De Niro.
fields.Works: Taxi Driver; Raging Bull; Goodfellas
fields.Notes: He won his only directing Oscar for The Departed in 2006, and has spent decades funding film preservation.

fields.Title: Andrei Tarkovsky
fields.Clue: A Russian who made only seven features, described his craft as “sculpting in time,” and died in exile in Paris in 1986.
fields.Works: Andrei Rublev; Solaris; Stalker
fields.Notes: His father was the poet Arseny Tarkovsky, whose verse is read aloud in several of the films.

fields.Title: David Lynch
fields.Clue: An Eagle Scout from Missoula whose films peel back the lawns of small-town America to show the beetles underneath.
fields.Works: Eraserhead; Blue Velvet; Mulholland Drive
fields.Notes: He also co-created Twin Peaks, and practised Transcendental Meditation for decades.

fields.Title: F. W. Murnau
fields.Clue: A German Expressionist who went to Hollywood and won a one-off Academy Award for Unique and Artistic Production.
fields.Works: Nosferatu; Sunrise
fields.Notes: He died in a car crash on the Pacific Coast Highway a week before the premiere of Tabu; eleven of his twenty-one films are lost.

fields.Title: Charlie Chaplin
fields.Clue: A London music-hall performer who became the most famous man on earth as a tramp in a bowler hat, and co-founded United Artists.
fields.Works: City Lights; Modern Times
fields.Notes: He was effectively exiled from the United States in 1952 over his politics and returned only in 1972 to collect an honorary Oscar.

fields.Title: Howard Hawks
fields.Clue: An Indiana-born professional who worked in every genre without a signature visual style, and whose women give as good as they get.
fields.Works: Bringing Up Baby; His Girl Friday
fields.Notes: He never won a competitive Oscar; the French critics of Cahiers du cinéma made the case for him as an author.

fields.Title: Orson Welles
fields.Clue: A prodigy who panicked radio listeners with a Martian invasion, and at twenty-five made a film that William Randolph Hearst tried to have destroyed.
fields.Works: Citizen Kane; Touch of Evil
fields.Notes: He acted in others' films to fund his own; The Other Side of the Wind was completed and released in 2018, 33 years after his death.

fields.Title: Akira Kurosawa
fields.Clue: The Japanese director who opened his country's cinema to the West, and whose swordsmen were remade as cowboys in Hollywood and Italy.
fields.Works: Rashomon; Seven Samurai
fields.Notes: He worked with Toshiro Mifune sixteen times; after a suicide attempt in 1971, his late films were funded from the Soviet Union, France, and America.

fields.Title: John Ford
fields.Clue: A Maine-born son of Irish immigrants who won four directing Oscars, none of them for his Westerns, and shot nine films in Monument Valley.
fields.Works: The Grapes of Wrath; The Searchers
fields.Notes: He filmed the Battle of Midway for the navy and was wounded doing it; John Wayne appeared in more than twenty of his films.

fields.Title: François Truffaut
fields.Clue: A Cahiers du cinéma critic who attacked French studio cinema in print, then launched the New Wave at Cannes with a semi-autobiographical first feature.
fields.Works: The 400 Blows; Jules and Jim
fields.Notes: He wrote the book-length interview with Alfred Hitchcock that changed how Hitchcock was regarded, and acted in Close Encounters of the Third Kind.

fields.Title: Francis Ford Coppola
fields.Clue: A UCLA film graduate who won Best Picture twice in three years, for a mafia saga and its sequel.
fields.Works: The Godfather; Apocalypse Now
fields.Notes: He won five Oscars; his wineries paid off his debts, and his daughter Sofia and nephew Nicolas Cage also went into film.

fields.Title: Werner Herzog
fields.Clue: A Bavarian who dragged a steamship over a hill in Peru, and narrates his documentaries in a flat, doom-laden voice.
fields.Works: Land of Silence and Darkness; Aguirre, the Wrath of God; Nosferatu the Vampyre; Fitzcarraldo; Grizzly Man
fields.Notes: He once ate his own shoe after losing a bet to Errol Morris, and walked from Munich to Paris believing it would keep Lotte Eisner alive.

fields.Title: Roman Polanski
fields.Clue: A survivor of the Kraków ghetto who fled the United States in 1978 after pleading guilty to unlawful sex with a thirteen-year-old.
fields.Works: Rosemary's Baby; Chinatown
fields.Notes: His wife Sharon Tate was murdered by the Manson family in 1969; he won the directing Oscar in absentia for The Pianist.

fields.Title: Ridley Scott
fields.Clue: A Tyneside-born maker of commercials whose two science-fiction films of 1979 and 1982 set the look of the genre for forty years.
fields.Works: Alien; Blade Runner
fields.Notes: He made the 1984 Apple advertisement; his brother Tony was also a director.

fields.Title: Wim Wenders
fields.Clue: A leading figure of New German Cinema whose films are mostly journeys, and who also made a documentary about Cuban musicians.
fields.Works: Paris, Texas; Wings of Desire
fields.Notes: He also photographs landscapes; Buena Vista Social Club and Pina were both nominated for documentary Oscars.

fields.Title: Quentin Tarantino
fields.Clue: A former video-store clerk whose films scramble chronology, quote genre cinema constantly, and use old records instead of a score.
fields.Works: Reservoir Dogs; Pulp Fiction
fields.Notes: He has won two screenplay Oscars; Reservoir Dogs was largely financed by Harvey Keitel after he read the script.

fields.Title: Joel and Ethan Coen
fields.Clue: Minnesota brothers who wrote, produced, and directed together for nearly forty years, and edited under the shared pseudonym Roderick Jaynes.
fields.Works: Blood Simple; Fargo
fields.Notes: No Country for Old Men won them Best Picture in 2008.
fields.Caption: Ethan (left) and Joel Coen at the Castro Theatre, San Francisco, 2016

fields.Title: Michael Haneke
fields.Clue: An Austrian who films violence as coldly as possible to deny the audience any pleasure in it, and has twice won the Palme d'Or.
fields.Works: Caché; The White Ribbon
fields.Notes: He remade his own Funny Games shot for shot in English ten years later; he taught directing in Vienna.

fields.Title: Alfonso Cuarón
fields.Clue: One of the three Mexican directors who dominated Hollywood's awards in the 2010s, and who wrote, photographed, and edited a film about his family's housekeeper.
fields.Works: Gravity; Roma
fields.Notes: He has won four Oscars; he also directed the third Harry Potter film, which is generally counted the best of them.

fields.Title: Peter Jackson
fields.Clue: A New Zealander who began with splatter comedies made on weekends, and filmed a three-part fantasy epic back to back in his own country.
fields.Works: Heavenly Creatures; The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
fields.Notes: He later restored and colourized First World War footage for They Shall Not Grow Old; his effects house is Weta.

fields.Title: David Lean
fields.Clue: An English editor turned director who made intimate British films in the 1940s, and then a run of enormous 70mm location epics.
fields.Works: Brief Encounter; Lawrence of Arabia
fields.Notes: He won two directing Oscars; his early Dickens adaptations are still the standard ones.

fields.Title: Robert Altman
fields.Clue: A Kansas City bomber pilot who came to features late, and filled them with overlapping multitrack dialogue, huge casts, and zoom lenses.
fields.Works: Nashville; Short Cuts
fields.Notes: He never won a competitive Oscar and said so at the podium when given an honorary one in 2006.

fields.Title: Paul Thomas Anderson
fields.Clue: A San Fernando Valley director who moved from sprawling ensembles to close studies of monstrous men, with Jonny Greenwood scoring most of his films since 2007.
fields.Works: There Will Be Blood; Phantom Thread
fields.Notes: Boogie Nights and Magnolia are the sprawling ensembles; The Master is his portrait of a cult leader.

fields.Title: Jean-Luc Godard
fields.Clue: The most radical of the Cahiers du cinéma critics turned director, who invented the jump cut to shorten his first feature.
fields.Works: Breathless
fields.Notes: He chose assisted suicide in Switzerland in 2022; his 1960s films with Anna Karina are the ones most often shown.

fields.Title: Agnès Varda
fields.Clue: A Belgian-born photographer called the grandmother of the New Wave, who in her seventies made a documentary about gleaners on a handheld camera.
fields.Works: Cléo from 5 to 7
fields.Notes: She was married to Jacques Demy, and received an honorary Oscar in 2017.

fields.Title: Yasujirō Ozu
fields.Clue: A Japanese director who returned throughout his career to parents, grown children, and a daughter who will not marry, filmed from the height of someone kneeling on a tatami mat.
fields.Works: Tokyo Story
fields.Notes: He was born and died on the same date, 12 December; his gravestone at Engaku-ji carries the single character for nothingness.
fields.Caption: Ozu (right, in his white hat) with Setsuko Hara on the set of Tokyo Story

fields.Title: Bong Joon-ho
fields.Clue: A South Korean who mixes genre and class satire without warning, and took four Oscars in one night in 2020.
fields.Works: Parasite
fields.Notes: Accepting a Golden Globe in 2020, he said that subtitles are a one-inch barrier worth getting over.

fields.Title: Jean Renoir
fields.Clue: The painter's son who made the two towering films of French poetic realism, and spent the war years in Hollywood.
fields.Works: The Rules of the Game
fields.Notes: His father was Pierre-Auguste Renoir; he acted in his own films, most memorably as Octave.

fields.Title: Satyajit Ray
fields.Clue: A Calcutta commercial artist who saw Bicycle Thieves in London, and sold his wife's jewellery to fund his first feature.
fields.Works: Pather Panchali
fields.Notes: He also wrote detective fiction and composed his own scores; he received an honorary Oscar weeks before his death.

fields.Title: L'Avventura
fields.Cast: Monica Vitti; Gabriele Ferzetti; Lea Massari
fields.Clue: On a yachting trip to a volcanic island a woman vanishes, and her lover and her best friend drift into an affair instead of finding her.
fields.Notes: Booed at Cannes, then given a special jury prize; the first of Antonioni's trilogy with Monica Vitti, followed by La Notte and L'Eclisse.

fields.Title: Blowup
fields.Cast: David Hemmings; Vanessa Redgrave; Sarah Miles
fields.Clue: A fashion photographer in Swinging London enlarges his pictures of a park until they seem to show a body in the bushes.
fields.Notes: Antonioni's first English-language film, from a Julio Cortázar story; it ends with mimes playing tennis without a ball.

fields.Title: Grand Illusion
fields.Cast: Jean Gabin; Pierre Fresnay; Erich von Stroheim
fields.Clue: French officers in a First World War prison camp plan escapes while the aristocratic German commandant befriends the one captain of his own class.
fields.Notes: Von Stroheim plays the commandant, von Rauffenstein. Goebbels called it “cinematic public enemy number one”, and the Germans seized the negative in 1940.

fields.Title: The Great Dictator
fields.Cast: Charlie Chaplin; Paulette Goddard; Jack Oakie
fields.Clue: A Jewish barber is mistaken for his double, Adenoid Hynkel, the dictator of Tomainia.
fields.Notes: Chaplin's first true talkie, in which Hynkel dances with an inflatable globe; Chaplin later said he could not have made it had he known of the camps.

fields.Title: It Happened One Night
fields.Cast: Clark Gable; Claudette Colbert
fields.Clue: A runaway heiress and a newspaperman hang a blanket, the “Walls of Jericho”, between their motel beds.
fields.Notes: The first film to win all five major Academy Awards, since matched only by One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest and The Silence of the Lambs.

fields.Title: The Bridge on the River Kwai
fields.Cast: Alec Guinness; William Holden; Sessue Hayakawa
fields.Clue: A British colonel in a Japanese prison camp in Burma drives his men to build a railway bridge properly, as a point of pride.
fields.Notes: The blacklisted writers Carl Foreman and Michael Wilson went uncredited, so the Oscar for the script went to Pierre Boulle, who wrote the novel.

fields.Title: Cries and Whispers
fields.Cast: Harriet Andersson; Ingrid Thulin; Liv Ullmann; Kari Sylwan
fields.Clue: Two sisters and a maid keep watch over a third sister dying of cancer in a manor house of blood-red rooms.
fields.Notes: Sven Nykvist's colour photography won the Academy Award; Bergman said he pictured the inside of the soul as a red membrane.

fields.Title: Ran
fields.Cast: Tatsuya Nakadai; Akira Terao; Jinpachi Nezu; Mieko Harada
fields.Clue: An old warlord, Hidetora Ichimonji, divides his domain among his three sons, who turn on him.
fields.Notes: King Lear with sons for daughters; Kurosawa's last epic, made with French money after Japanese studios would not fund it.

fields.Title: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
fields.Cast: Clint Eastwood; Lee Van Cleef; Eli Wallach
fields.Clue: Three gunmen race through the Civil War after Confederate gold buried in a cemetery, and settle it in a three-way standoff.
fields.Notes: The last of Leone's Dollars trilogy with Eastwood as the Man with No Name; Ennio Morricone's theme imitates a coyote's howl.

fields.Title: Chungking Express
fields.Cast: Tony Leung; Faye Wong; Takeshi Kaneshiro; Brigitte Lin
fields.Clue: A jilted Hong Kong policeman buys tins of pineapple that expire on the first of May, his birthday.
fields.Notes: Shot in about two months while Wong was stuck editing Ashes of Time; Faye Wong plays “California Dreamin'” over and over.

fields.Title: Sátántangó
fields.Cast: Mihály Víg; Putyi Horváth; Erika Bók
fields.Clue: A seven-hour film of a collapsing collective farm, in twelve parts that step forward and back like a tango.
fields.Notes: From László Krasznahorkai's novel; it opens with a single take of cows wandering out of a barn.

fields.Title: Koyaanisqatsi
fields.Clue: A wordless film of time-lapse deserts and city crowds, its Hopi title meaning “life out of balance”.
fields.Notes: Philip Glass wrote the score and Ron Fricke shot it; the first of Reggio's Qatsi trilogy.

fields.Title: Touki Bouki
fields.Cast: Magaye Niang; Mareme Niang
fields.Clue: A cowherd whose motorbike wears a zebu's horns and his girlfriend scheme their way out of Dakar toward Paris.
fields.Notes: Restored by Martin Scorsese's World Cinema Foundation in 2008, and often named the greatest African film.

fields.Title: Man with a Movie Camera
fields.Clue: A day of Soviet city life with no story, actors, or intertitles, which keeps showing its own cameraman and editor at work.
fields.Notes: Vertov's kino-eye made the camera a better eye than the human one; it topped Sight and Sound's 2014 poll of documentaries.

fields.Title: Michelangelo Antonioni
fields.Clue: The Italian director of alienation whose films with Monica Vitti end in empty streets and disappearances nobody solves.
fields.Works: L'Avventura; La Notte; L'Eclisse; Blowup
fields.Notes: Blowup was his first film in English; Zabriskie Point ends with a house exploding in slow motion.

fields.Title: Buster Keaton
fields.Clue: The “Great Stone Face” of silent comedy, who stood still while the front of a house fell around him.
fields.Works: Sherlock Jr.; The General; Steamboat Bill, Jr.
fields.Notes: He did his own stunts; The General, his Civil War locomotive chase, flopped in 1926 and now ranks among the greatest films.

fields.Title: Pier Paolo Pasolini
fields.Clue: The Italian poet and director killed on the beach at Ostia weeks before his adaptation of Sade, Salò, came out.
fields.Works: Accattone; The Gospel According to St. Matthew; Salò, or the 120 Days of Sodom
fields.Notes: A Marxist raised Catholic, he cast his own mother as the aged Mary in his Gospel.

fields.Title: Erich von Stroheim
fields.Clue: The Vienna-born director whose Greed ran about nine hours before MGM cut it to two.
fields.Works: Foolish Wives; Greed; Queen Kelly
fields.Notes: Later an actor: the commandant in Grand Illusion and the butler Max in Sunset Boulevard.

fields.Title: Max Ophüls
fields.Clue: The German-born director of long gliding tracking shots through ballrooms and waltzes.
fields.Works: Letter from an Unknown Woman; La Ronde; The Earrings of Madame de…; Lola Montès
fields.Notes: He worked in Germany, France, and Hollywood; his son Marcel made The Sorrow and the Pity.

fields.Title: Clint Eastwood
fields.Clue: The Man with No Name in Leone's westerns, who directed himself as a retired gunfighter in Unforgiven.
fields.Works: Unforgiven; Mystic River; Million Dollar Baby; Letters from Iwo Jima
fields.Notes: Unforgiven and Million Dollar Baby each won him Best Picture and Best Director.

fields.Title: Marilyn Monroe
fields.Clue: Her white dress billowed up over a subway grate in The Seven Year Itch.
fields.Works: Gentlemen Prefer Blondes; Some Like It Hot; The Misfits
fields.Notes: Born Norma Jeane Mortenson; she sang “Happy Birthday, Mr. President” to Kennedy in 1962, and Warhol silkscreened her face after her death.

fields.Title: Toshiro Mifune
fields.Clue: The Japanese actor who played the bandit Tajōmaru and the would-be samurai Kikuchiyo for Kurosawa.
fields.Works: Rashomon; Seven Samurai; Throne of Blood; Yojimbo
fields.Notes: He made sixteen films with Kurosawa; for the end of Throne of Blood, real arrows were shot at him.

fields.Title: Audrey Hepburn
fields.Clue: She ate a pastry outside Tiffany's window as Holly Golightly.
fields.Works: Roman Holiday; Sabrina; Breakfast at Tiffany's; My Fair Lady
fields.Notes: Born in Brussels, she won the Academy Award for her first starring role, in Roman Holiday, and spent her last years working for UNICEF.

fields.Title: Ingrid Bergman
fields.Clue: She played Ilsa Lund, who asks Sam to play “As Time Goes By” in Casablanca.
fields.Works: Casablanca; Gaslight; Notorious; Autumn Sonata
fields.Notes: Her affair with Roberto Rossellini during Stromboli was denounced on the floor of the U.S. Senate; she won three Academy Awards.

fields.Title: Judy Garland
fields.Clue: She sang “Over the Rainbow” as Dorothy Gale.
fields.Works: The Wizard of Oz; Meet Me in St. Louis; A Star Is Born
fields.Notes: Born Frances Gumm; Liza Minnelli is her daughter with Vincente Minnelli, who directed Meet Me in St. Louis.

fields.Title: Marlene Dietrich
fields.Clue: She played the cabaret singer Lola Lola, who ruins a schoolteacher in The Blue Angel.
fields.Works: The Blue Angel; Morocco; Shanghai Express; Touch of Evil
fields.Notes: Seven films with Josef von Sternberg; she took American citizenship and entertained Allied troops at the front in the Second World War.

fields.Title: Marlon Brando
fields.Clue: He bellowed “Stella!” as Stanley Kowalski.
fields.Works: A Streetcar Named Desire; On the Waterfront; The Godfather; Apocalypse Now
fields.Notes: The leading screen exponent of Method acting; he declined his Academy Award for The Godfather and sent Sacheen Littlefeather in his place.

fields.Title: Laurence Olivier
fields.Clue: The English actor who directed himself in Shakespeare films of Henry V, Hamlet, and Richard III.
fields.Works: Wuthering Heights; Rebecca; Hamlet; Richard III
fields.Notes: His Hamlet was the first film from outside the United States to win Best Picture; he was the first director of the National Theatre, and married Vivien Leigh.

fields.Title: Shirley Temple
fields.Clue: The child star who sang “On the Good Ship Lollipop” in Bright Eyes.
fields.Works: Bright Eyes; Curly Top; Heidi
fields.Notes: Given a special juvenile Academy Award at six, she later served as ambassador to Ghana and to Czechoslovakia as Shirley Temple Black.

fields.Title: Greta Garbo
fields.Clue: The Swedish star who says “I want to be alone” in Grand Hotel.
fields.Works: Anna Christie; Grand Hotel; Queen Christina; Ninotchka
fields.Notes: Publicity ran “Garbo talks!” for Anna Christie and “Garbo laughs!” for Ninotchka; she retired at thirty-six.

fields.Title: Daniel Day-Lewis
fields.Clue: The only man to win three Academy Awards for Best Actor.
fields.Works: My Left Foot; There Will Be Blood; Lincoln; Phantom Thread
fields.Notes: Known for staying in character through whole shoots; he played Christy Brown, Daniel Plainview, and Abraham Lincoln.

fields.Title: Robert De Niro
fields.Clue: He asked “You talkin' to me?” into a mirror as Travis Bickle.
fields.Works: Taxi Driver; The Godfather Part II; Raging Bull; Goodfellas
fields.Notes: He starred in ten features for Martin Scorsese, and gained about sixty pounds to play the older Jake LaMotta in Raging Bull.

fields.Title: Rita Hayworth
fields.Clue: She peeled off a long black glove singing “Put the Blame on Mame” in Gilda.
fields.Works: Only Angels Have Wings; Cover Girl; Gilda; The Lady from Shanghai
fields.Notes: A pin-up of the Second World War; she married Orson Welles, who cut and bleached her hair for The Lady from Shanghai.

fields.Title: Jack Nicholson
fields.Clue: He played Randle McMurphy against Nurse Ratched in One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest.
fields.Works: Easy Rider; Chinatown; One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest; The Shining
fields.Notes: Nominated for twelve Academy Awards, the most of any male actor; he improvised “Here's Johnny!” in The Shining.

fields.Title: Mae West
fields.Clue: She asked a young Cary Grant to “come up sometime and see me” in She Done Him Wrong.
fields.Works: She Done Him Wrong; I'm No Angel; My Little Chickadee
fields.Notes: Sentenced to ten days in jail in 1927 over her Broadway play Sex; Second World War airmen called their inflatable life vests Mae Wests.

fields.Title: Katharine Hepburn
fields.Clue: The actor with the most Academy Awards for acting: four, all for Best Actress.
fields.Works: Bringing Up Baby; The Philadelphia Story; The African Queen; Guess Who's Coming to Dinner
fields.Notes: She made nine films with Spencer Tracy; labelled “box office poison” in 1938, she bought the film rights to The Philadelphia Story to come back.

fields.Title: Barbara Stanwyck
fields.Clue: As Phyllis Dietrichson she talks an insurance salesman into killing her husband in Double Indemnity.
fields.Works: Stella Dallas; The Lady Eve; Double Indemnity
fields.Notes: Nominated four times without winning, she received an honorary Academy Award in 1982.

fields.Title: Humphrey Bogart
fields.Clue: He played Rick Blaine, owner of Rick's Café Américain.
fields.Works: The Maltese Falcon; Casablanca; The Big Sleep; The African Queen
fields.Notes: First among AFI's male screen legends; he married Lauren Bacall after To Have and Have Not and won his Academy Award for The African Queen.

fields.Title: Cary Grant
fields.Clue: He ran from a crop-dusting plane across a cornfield in North by Northwest.
fields.Works: Bringing Up Baby; His Girl Friday; Notorious; North by Northwest
fields.Notes: Born Archibald Leach in Bristol; four films with Hitchcock, and an honorary Academy Award in 1970 after never winning a competitive one.

fields.Title: John Wayne
fields.Clue: He played Ethan Edwards, who searches for years for his kidnapped niece in The Searchers.
fields.Works: Stagecoach; Red River; The Searchers; True Grit
fields.Notes: Nicknamed the Duke; he made more than twenty films with John Ford, and won his Academy Award as Rooster Cogburn in True Grit.

fields.Title: Jacques Rivette
fields.Clue: The French New Wave director whose two heroines slip into a haunted house of repeating melodrama in Céline and Julie Go Boating.
fields.Works: Paris Belongs to Us; Céline and Julie Go Boating; Out 1; La Belle Noiseuse
fields.Notes: He edited Cahiers du cinéma from 1963 to 1965, and his films ran long: Out 1 lasts almost thirteen hours.

fields.Title: Terence Davies
fields.Clue: The Liverpool director who turned his Catholic working-class childhood into Distant Voices, Still Lives.
fields.Works: Distant Voices, Still Lives; The Long Day Closes; The House of Mirth; Benediction
fields.Notes: Popular songs carry his memory films; later he adapted Edith Wharton and filmed Siegfried Sassoon's life.

fields.Title: Lynne Ramsay
fields.Clue: The Glasgow director whose Ratcatcher follows a boy through the city's 1970s dustmen's strike.
fields.Works: Ratcatcher; Morvern Callar; We Need to Talk About Kevin; You Were Never Really Here
fields.Notes: Joaquin Phoenix plays a hammer-wielding rescuer in You Were Never Really Here, which won her the Cannes screenplay prize.

fields.Title: Miranda July
fields.Clue: The performance artist who wrote, directed, and starred in Me and You and Everyone We Know.
fields.Works: Me and You and Everyone We Know; The Future; Kajillionaire
fields.Notes: Her first feature won the Caméra d'Or at Cannes in 2005; she also wrote the novel All Fours (2024).

fields.Title: Max von Sydow
fields.Clue: He played the knight who plays chess with Death on a beach in The Seventh Seal.
fields.Works: The Seventh Seal; Wild Strawberries; The Virgin Spring; The Exorcist
fields.Notes: He made eleven films with Ingmar Bergman; in Hollywood he played Jesus in The Greatest Story Ever Told and Father Merrin in The Exorcist.

fields.Title: Marcello Mastroianni
fields.Clue: He played the jaded journalist who follows Anita Ekberg into the Trevi Fountain in La Dolce Vita.
fields.Works: La Dolce Vita; 8½; Divorce Italian Style; A Special Day
fields.Notes: Fellini's screen alter ego in La Dolce Vita and 8½, and Sophia Loren's most frequent partner; he was nominated three times for the Academy Award for Best Actor.

fields.Title: Peter Lorre
fields.Clue: He played the child murderer Hans Beckert, marked with a chalked letter, in Fritz Lang's M.
fields.Works: M; The Man Who Knew Too Much; The Maltese Falcon; Casablanca
fields.Notes: Born László Löwenstein; in Hollywood he played Joel Cairo in The Maltese Falcon and Ugarte in Casablanca, both opposite Humphrey Bogart.

fields.Title: Amitabh Bachchan
fields.Clue: The Hindi film star of the 1970s “angry young man” roles, who played Jai in Sholay.
fields.Works: Zanjeer; Deewaar; Sholay; Black
fields.Notes: Nicknamed “Big B”; from 2000 he hosted Kaun Banega Crorepati, India's Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?

fields.Title: Robert Bresson
fields.Clue: The French director who called his non-professional actors “models” and set down his method in Notes on the Cinematograph.
fields.Works: A Man Escaped; Pickpocket; Au Hasard Balthazar; Mouchette
fields.Notes: Au Hasard Balthazar follows a donkey through a string of owners; his last film was L'Argent (1983).

fields.Title: Carl Theodor Dreyer
fields.Clue: The Danish director who filmed Renée Falconetti in close-up after close-up as Joan of Arc on trial.
fields.Works: The Passion of Joan of Arc; Vampyr; Day of Wrath; Ordet
fields.Notes: Ordet ends with a woman raised from the dead in her coffin; Gertrud (1964) was his last film.

fields.Title: Kenji Mizoguchi
fields.Clue: The Japanese director of long single takes whose films return again and again to women sold or ruined by men.
fields.Works: The Life of Oharu; Ugetsu; Sansho the Bailiff; Street of Shame
fields.Notes: Ugetsu, in which a potter is seduced by a ghostly noblewoman, and Sansho the Bailiff won Silver Lions at Venice in successive years.

fields.Title: Roberto Rossellini
fields.Clue: His Rome, Open City, shot in a city just freed from German occupation, launched Italian Neorealism.
fields.Works: Rome, Open City; Paisan; Germany, Year Zero; Journey to Italy
fields.Notes: He made five films with Ingrid Bergman, beginning with Stromboli, during an affair that scandalized Hollywood; Isabella Rossellini is their daughter.

fields.Title: Chantal Akerman
fields.Clue: The Belgian director whose three-hour study of a widow's household routine topped the 2022 Sight and Sound critics' poll.
fields.Works: Je, tu, il, elle; Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles; News from Home; No Home Movie
fields.Notes: Delphine Seyrig plays Jeanne Dielman, whose days of cooking, cleaning, and sex work slowly unravel; Akerman made it in her mid-twenties.

fields.Title: Sergei Eisenstein
fields.Clue: The Soviet director and theorist of montage who staged a massacre on the Odessa Steps.
fields.Works: Strike; Battleship Potemkin; October; Alexander Nevsky; Ivan the Terrible
fields.Notes: Prokofiev scored Alexander Nevsky and Ivan the Terrible; Stalin banned Part II of Ivan.

fields.Title: Wong Kar-wai
fields.Clue: The Hong Kong director, never without dark glasses, of slow-motion longing in neon-lit apartments and noodle stalls.
fields.Works: Chungking Express; Fallen Angels; Happy Together; In the Mood for Love
fields.Notes: Christopher Doyle shot most of his films; Tony Leung and Maggie Cheung play the neighbours of In the Mood for Love.

fields.Title: Abbas Kiarostami
fields.Clue: The Iranian director of zigzag mountain roads, whose Koker trilogy began with a boy trying to return a classmate's notebook.
fields.Works: Where Is the Friend's House?; Close-Up; Taste of Cherry; Certified Copy
fields.Notes: Taste of Cherry, about a man looking for someone to bury him after his suicide, shared the 1997 Palme d'Or.

fields.Title: Vittorio De Sica
fields.Clue: The Italian actor-director who cast a factory worker as the bill-poster searching Rome for his stolen bicycle.
fields.Works: Shoeshine; Bicycle Thieves; Umberto D.; Two Women
fields.Notes: Four of his films won the Academy Award for foreign-language film; Sophia Loren won Best Actress for Two Women.

fields.Title: John Cassavetes
fields.Clue: The actor who financed his own raw, improvised-seeming films, beginning with Shadows, often starring his wife, Gena Rowlands.
fields.Works: Shadows; Faces; A Woman Under the Influence; Opening Night
fields.Notes: Called the father of American independent film; he paid for his work by acting, as in Rosemary's Baby and The Dirty Dozen.

fields.Title: Luchino Visconti
fields.Clue: The aristocratic Marxist director whose The Leopard follows a Sicilian prince through the Risorgimento.
fields.Works: Ossessione; La Terra Trema; Rocco and His Brothers; The Leopard; Death in Venice
fields.Notes: Ossessione, an unauthorized The Postman Always Rings Twice, anticipated Neorealism; Burt Lancaster plays the prince in The Leopard.

fields.Title: Ernst Lubitsch
fields.Clue: The Berlin-born Hollywood director whose sly, suggestive comedies gave rise to a “touch” named after him.
fields.Works: Trouble in Paradise; Ninotchka; The Shop Around the Corner; To Be or Not to Be
fields.Notes: To Be or Not to Be, a comedy of Polish actors fooling the Nazis, outraged audiences in 1942; Billy Wilder kept a sign asking “How would Lubitsch do it?”

fields.Title: Woody Allen
fields.Clue: The New York comic who won Best Director for a romance with Diane Keaton that ends with her moving to Los Angeles.
fields.Works: Annie Hall; Manhattan; Hannah and Her Sisters; Crimes and Misdemeanors
fields.Notes: He holds the record of sixteen nominations for the screenwriting Academy Award.

fields.Title: Alain Resnais
fields.Clue: The French Left Bank director who intercut an actress's wartime memories with her affair with a Japanese architect.
fields.Works: Night and Fog; Hiroshima mon amour; Last Year at Marienbad; Providence
fields.Notes: Marguerite Duras wrote Hiroshima mon amour and Alain Robbe-Grillet Last Year at Marienbad.

fields.Title: Sergio Leone
fields.Clue: The Italian director of spaghetti westerns who made Clint Eastwood the Man with No Name.
fields.Works: A Fistful of Dollars; The Good, the Bad and the Ugly; Once Upon a Time in the West; Once Upon a Time in America
fields.Notes: Ennio Morricone scored all his westerns; A Fistful of Dollars remade Kurosawa's Yojimbo without permission.

fields.Title: Stanley Donen
fields.Clue: He co-directed Singin' in the Rain with its star, Gene Kelly.
fields.Works: On the Town; Singin' in the Rain; Funny Face; Charade
fields.Notes: A former Broadway dancer; Charade, with Cary Grant and Audrey Hepburn, is often called the best Hitchcock film Hitchcock didn't make.

fields.Title: Jean Vigo
fields.Clue: The French director who died of tuberculosis at twenty-nine, leaving a featurette of a boarding-school revolt and a feature set on a barge.
fields.Works: À propos de Nice; Zero for Conduct; L'Atalante
fields.Notes: Zero for Conduct was banned in France until 1945; the Prix Jean Vigo is named after him.

fields.Title: Rainer Werner Fassbinder
fields.Clue: The New German Cinema director who reworked Sirk's All That Heaven Allows as a romance between a cleaning woman and a Moroccan worker.
fields.Works: Ali: Fear Eats the Soul; The Bitter Tears of Petra von Kant; The Marriage of Maria Braun; Berlin Alexanderplatz
fields.Notes: He made more than forty films in about fifteen years before dying at thirty-seven.

fields.Title: Terrence Malick
fields.Clue: The former philosophy lecturer who shot Days of Heaven almost entirely at magic hour, then made no film for twenty years.
fields.Works: Badlands; Days of Heaven; The Thin Red Line; The Tree of Life
fields.Notes: He translated Heidegger before turning to film; The Tree of Life won the 2011 Palme d'Or.

fields.Title: Jacques Tati
fields.Clue: The French comic who played the pipe-smoking, raincoated Monsieur Hulot.
fields.Works: Jour de fête; Monsieur Hulot's Holiday; Mon Oncle; Playtime
fields.Notes: He built a glass-and-steel city set for Playtime, nicknamed Tativille; its cost bankrupted him.

fields.Title: Chris Marker
fields.Clue: The French essay filmmaker whose short science-fiction film is told almost entirely in still photographs.
fields.Works: La Jetée; Sans Soleil; A Grin Without a Cat
fields.Notes: He avoided being photographed and sent a cat instead, often Guillaume-en-Égypte, the grinning cartoon cat who was his alter ego; La Jetée inspired 12 Monkeys.
fields.Caption: Marker hidden behind his camera: he rarely let himself be photographed, and often sent a picture of a cat instead

fields.Title: Dziga Vertov
fields.Clue: The Soviet documentarist of the “kino-eye”, whose city symphony keeps showing its own cameraman and editor at work.
fields.Works: Kino-Pravda; Man with a Movie Camera; Enthusiasm; Three Songs About Lenin
fields.Notes: Born David Kaufman; his brother Mikhail shot Man with a Movie Camera, and his wife, Elizaveta Svilova, edited it.

fields.Title: Hou Hsiao-hsien
fields.Clue: The Taiwanese New Wave director whose A City of Sadness broke the silence about the 228 Incident.
fields.Works: The Time to Live and the Time to Die; A City of Sadness; The Puppetmaster; The Assassin
fields.Notes: A City of Sadness won the Golden Lion in 1989; The Assassin won him Best Director at Cannes in 2015.

fields.Title: Krzysztof Kieślowski
fields.Clue: The Polish director of ten television films on the Ten Commandments, set in one Warsaw housing estate.
fields.Works: Dekalog; The Double Life of Véronique; Three Colours: Blue; Three Colours: Red
fields.Notes: The Three Colours trilogy takes the French flag's liberty, equality, and fraternity; Irène Jacob stars in Véronique and Red.

fields.Title: Claire Denis
fields.Clue: The French director, raised in colonial Africa, who restaged Billy Budd among Foreign Legionnaires in Djibouti.
fields.Works: Chocolat; Beau Travail; 35 Shots of Rum; High Life
fields.Notes: Beau Travail ends with Denis Lavant dancing alone to “The Rhythm of the Night”.

fields.Title: D. W. Griffith
fields.Clue: The pioneer of the close-up and cross-cutting whose Civil War epic glorified the Ku Klux Klan.
fields.Works: The Birth of a Nation; Intolerance; Broken Blossoms; Way Down East
fields.Notes: He co-founded United Artists with Chaplin, Mary Pickford, and Douglas Fairbanks; Lillian Gish starred in many of his films.

fields.Title: Frank Capra
fields.Clue: The Sicilian-born director of populist fables, from a naive senator's filibuster to a small-town banker saved by an angel.
fields.Works: It Happened One Night; Mr. Deeds Goes to Town; Mr. Smith Goes to Washington; It's a Wonderful Life
fields.Notes: He won Best Director three times in the 1930s, and made the Why We Fight series in the Second World War.

fields.Title: Hayao Miyazaki
fields.Clue: The co-founder of Studio Ghibli who directed a girl's year working in a bathhouse for spirits.
fields.Works: My Neighbor Totoro; Princess Mononoke; Spirited Away; The Boy and the Heron
fields.Notes: Spirited Away and The Boy and the Heron both won the Academy Award for Animated Feature.

fields.Title: Sam Peckinpah
fields.Clue: The director nicknamed “Bloody Sam” for the slow-motion gunfights of his westerns.
fields.Works: Ride the High Country; The Wild Bunch; Straw Dogs; Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid
fields.Notes: The Wild Bunch ends in a massacre in a Mexican town; Bob Dylan wrote “Knockin' on Heaven's Door” for Pat Garrett.

fields.Title: Douglas Sirk
fields.Clue: The German émigré whose lush Universal melodramas, often with Rock Hudson, were later read as critiques of American life.
fields.Works: Magnificent Obsession; All That Heaven Allows; Written on the Wind; Imitation of Life
fields.Notes: Born Hans Detlef Sierck; Fassbinder (Ali: Fear Eats the Soul) and Todd Haynes (Far from Heaven) reworked All That Heaven Allows.
fields.Caption: Sirk (left) with Jeff Chandler on the set of Sign of the Pagan, 1954

fields.Title: Spike Lee
fields.Clue: The Brooklyn director who played Mookie, the pizza delivery man who throws a trash can through Sal's window.
fields.Works: She's Gotta Have It; Do the Right Thing; Malcolm X; BlacKkKlansman
fields.Notes: His company is 40 Acres and a Mule Filmworks; he won the adapted-screenplay Academy Award for BlacKkKlansman.

fields.Title: Lars von Trier
fields.Clue: The Danish co-founder of the Dogme 95 movement, whose Breaking the Waves made Emily Watson a star.
fields.Works: Breaking the Waves; Dancer in the Dark; Dogville; Melancholia
fields.Notes: Dancer in the Dark, with Björk, won the 2000 Palme d'Or; Cannes declared him persona non grata in 2011.

fields.Title: Miloš Forman
fields.Clue: The Czech New Wave director who emigrated and won Best Director for Ken Kesey's novel of a mental hospital.
fields.Works: The Firemen's Ball; One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest; Hair; Amadeus
fields.Notes: Both One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest and Amadeus won Best Picture and Best Director.

fields.Title: Jane Campion
fields.Clue: The New Zealand director of a mute Scottish pianist who arrives in the colony with her daughter.
fields.Works: An Angel at My Table; The Piano; Bright Star; The Power of the Dog
fields.Notes: The first woman to win the Palme d'Or, for The Piano (1993); she won Best Director for The Power of the Dog.

fields.Title: Preston Sturges
fields.Clue: The screenwriter who became one of the first to direct his own scripts, satirizing a comedy director who sets out to suffer like the poor.
fields.Works: The Lady Eve; Sullivan's Travels; The Palm Beach Story; The Miracle of Morgan's Creek
fields.Notes: He won the first Academy Award for Original Screenplay, for The Great McGinty (1940).

fields.Title: Elia Kazan
fields.Clue: The director who named names to the House Un-American Activities Committee, then made a film about a dockworker who informs.
fields.Works: A Streetcar Named Desire; On the Waterfront; East of Eden; A Face in the Crowd
fields.Notes: He co-founded the Actors Studio; his 1999 honorary Academy Award drew protests inside and outside the hall.

fields.Title: Jean-Pierre Melville
fields.Clue: The French director of laconic gangster films whose hitman keeps a caged bullfinch in Le Samouraï.
fields.Works: Bob le flambeur; Le Samouraï; Army of Shadows; Le Cercle Rouge
fields.Notes: Born Jean-Pierre Grumbach, he took his name from the author of Moby-Dick; the New Wave treated him as a model.

fields.Title: Pedro Almodóvar
fields.Clue: The Spanish director who came out of Madrid's post-Franco Movida, with melodramas in saturated colour.
fields.Works: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown; All About My Mother; Talk to Her; Volver
fields.Notes: All About My Mother won the foreign-language Academy Award and Talk to Her the original-screenplay award; Penélope Cruz and Antonio Banderas are frequent stars.

fields.Title: Brian De Palma
fields.Clue: The New Hollywood director of split screens and Hitchcock homages, from a telekinetic prom queen to Tony Montana.
fields.Works: Carrie; Dressed to Kill; Scarface; The Untouchables
fields.Notes: The Untouchables restages the Odessa Steps sequence of Battleship Potemkin with a baby carriage in Union Station.

fields.Title: Sidney Lumet
fields.Clue: The director of a jury room in which one holdout talks eleven others out of a guilty verdict.
fields.Works: 12 Angry Men; Serpico; Dog Day Afternoon; Network
fields.Notes: Network gave Peter Finch “I'm as mad as hell, and I'm not going to take this anymore!”; he received an honorary Academy Award in 2005.

fields.Title: John Carpenter
fields.Clue: The director, who composes his own scores, of a masked killer stalking babysitters in Haddonfield, Illinois.
fields.Works: Assault on Precinct 13; Halloween; The Thing; They Live
fields.Notes: The Thing, his remake of a 1951 film, flopped on release and became a classic.

fields.Title: Ousmane Sembène
fields.Clue: The Senegalese novelist and director called the father of African cinema.
fields.Works: Black Girl; Mandabi; Xala; Moolaadé
fields.Notes: Black Girl (1966), about a Senegalese maid in France, is often called the first sub-Saharan African feature; he had worked as a docker in Marseille.

fields.Title: George Lucas
fields.Clue: The director of American Graffiti, who founded Industrial Light & Magic to make his space opera.
fields.Works: THX 1138; American Graffiti; Star Wars
fields.Notes: Joseph Campbell's The Hero with a Thousand Faces shaped Star Wars; he sold Lucasfilm to Disney in 2012.

fields.Title: Jean Cocteau
fields.Clue: The French poet and artist who directed Jean Marais as the Beast and as a poet led through a mirror into the underworld.
fields.Works: The Blood of a Poet; Beauty and the Beast; Orpheus; Testament of Orpheus
fields.Notes: He wrote Les Enfants Terribles and the scenario for the ballet Parade.

fields.Title: Mike Nichols
fields.Clue: The improv comedian, partner of Elaine May, who directed Dustin Hoffman's affair with Mrs. Robinson.
fields.Works: Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?; The Graduate; Carnal Knowledge; Working Girl
fields.Notes: One of the few to win an Emmy, a Grammy, an Oscar, and a Tony; the Oscar was Best Director for The Graduate.

fields.Title: Ang Lee
fields.Clue: The Taiwanese director of swordfights on bamboo treetops and of two cowboys' secret love.
fields.Works: Sense and Sensibility; Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon; Brokeback Mountain; Life of Pi
fields.Notes: He won Best Director twice, for Brokeback Mountain and Life of Pi.

fields.Title: Wes Anderson
fields.Clue: The director of symmetrical pastel tableaux, from a family of fallen prodigies to a concierge at a mountain hotel.
fields.Works: Rushmore; The Royal Tenenbaums; Fantastic Mr. Fox; The Grand Budapest Hotel
fields.Notes: Bill Murray appears in nearly all his films; his first Academy Award was for the short The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar.

fields.Title: Maya Deren
fields.Clue: The avant-garde filmmaker who, with her husband Alexander Hammid, made a dream film of keys, knives, and a hooded figure with a mirror for a face.
fields.Works: Meshes of the Afternoon; At Land; Ritual in Transfigured Time
fields.Notes: Born in Kyiv; she studied Vodou in Haiti for Divine Horsemen.

fields.Title: Louis Malle
fields.Clue: The French director whose Au revoir les enfants recalls a Jewish boy hidden at his Catholic boarding school.
fields.Works: Elevator to the Gallows; The Lovers; Au revoir les enfants; My Dinner with Andre
fields.Notes: Miles Davis improvised the score of Elevator to the Gallows; he married Candice Bergen.

fields.Title: Kelly Reichardt
fields.Clue: The American independent director of the Oregon frontier, from a lost wagon train to two men stealing milk for oily cakes.
fields.Works: Old Joy; Wendy and Lucy; Meek's Cutoff; First Cow
fields.Notes: Jon Raymond co-writes most of her films; Michelle Williams has starred in four of them.

fields.Title: Sofia Coppola
fields.Clue: The director who paired Bill Murray and Scarlett Johansson in a Tokyo hotel.
fields.Works: The Virgin Suicides; Lost in Translation; Marie Antoinette; The Beguiled
fields.Notes: Francis Ford Coppola's daughter, she played the baby in the christening scene of The Godfather; she won the original-screenplay Academy Award for Lost in Translation.

fields.Title: Derek Jarman
fields.Clue: The English director whose last film is a single blue screen with voices, made as he went blind with AIDS.
fields.Works: Sebastiane; Jubilee; Caravaggio; Blue
fields.Notes: A painter and set designer too; he made a celebrated garden of shingle and driftwood at Prospect Cottage, Dungeness.

fields.Title: Guillermo del Toro
fields.Clue: The Mexican director of a girl who meets a faun in the woods in Franco's Spain.
fields.Works: The Devil's Backbone; Pan's Labyrinth; The Shape of Water; Pinocchio
fields.Notes: The Shape of Water won Best Picture and Best Director; his Pinocchio won the animated-feature Academy Award.

fields.Title: Fantasia
fields.Cast: Leopold Stokowski; Deems Taylor
fields.Clue: Leopold Stokowski conducts the Philadelphia Orchestra in eight animated segments, among them dinosaurs to The Rite of Spring and an apprentice who loses control of an enchanted broom.
fields.Still caption: Mickey Mouse as the sorcerer's apprentice
fields.Notes: Released in Fantasound, an early multichannel stereo system; it lost money at first, and Deems Taylor introduces each piece.

fields.Title: 12 Angry Men
fields.Cast: Henry Fonda; Lee J. Cobb
fields.Clue: Juror 8 alone votes to acquit a teenager accused of stabbing his father, and one by one turns the other eleven in a sweltering jury room.
fields.Still caption: The jurors deliberate
fields.Notes: Lumet's first feature, adapted by Reginald Rose from his own 1954 television play; nearly all of it takes place in one room.

fields.Title: Ben-Hur
fields.Cast: Charlton Heston; Stephen Boyd
fields.Clue: A Jewish prince sent to the galleys by his boyhood friend Messala survives to take revenge on him in a nine-minute chariot race.
fields.Still caption: Charlton Heston and Stephen Boyd
fields.Notes: Its eleven Academy Awards set a record later matched by Titanic and The Return of the King; adapted from Lew Wallace's 1880 novel.
fields.Still 2 caption: Charlton Heston aboard the Roman galley

fields.Title: The Corbett–Fitzsimmons Fight
fields.Cast: James J. Corbett; Bob Fitzsimmons
fields.Clue: Shot at Carson City, Nevada, by three cameras side by side on wide film, this record of a heavyweight title bout ran about ninety minutes, the longest film yet made.
fields.Still caption: The ring at Carson City, 17 March 1897
fields.Notes: Often called the first feature-length film; only fragments survive.

fields.Title: The Birth of a Nation
fields.Cast: Lillian Gish; Henry B. Walthall
fields.Clue: Adapted from Thomas Dixon Jr.'s The Clansman, it follows two families through the Civil War and Reconstruction and glorifies the Ku Klux Klan, whose revival it helped inspire.
fields.Still caption: A Civil War battle scene
fields.Notes: Woodrow Wilson screened it at the White House and the NAACP protested it; its cross-cutting and close-ups made it a landmark of film grammar.

fields.Title: The Thief of Bagdad
fields.Cast: Douglas Fairbanks; Anna May Wong
fields.Clue: Douglas Fairbanks's rogue Ahmed, in love with the caliph's daughter, rides a flying carpet and a winged horse to win her, in a vast Arabian Nights city designed by William Cameron Menzies.
fields.Still caption: A scene in the caliph's palace
fields.Notes: One of the costliest films of the 1920s, at over a million dollars; Anna May Wong plays a Mongol slave.

fields.Title: The Phantom of the Opera
fields.Cast: Lon Chaney; Mary Philbin
fields.Clue: Christine Daaé tears the mask from the skull-like face of Erik, who haunts the cellars and underground lake of the Palais Garnier; its star designed the make-up himself.
fields.Still caption: Lon Chaney unmasked
fields.Notes: Adapted from Gaston Leroux's novel; its masked ball was shot in early two-strip Technicolor.
fields.Still 2 caption: The masked ball, in two-strip Technicolor

fields.Title: Georges Méliès
fields.Clue: The stage magician of the Théâtre Robert-Houdin who discovered the stop trick and filled his glass studio at Montreuil with trick films.
fields.Works: A Trip to the Moon; The Impossible Voyage; The Conquest of the Pole
fields.Notes: Ruined by 1913, he was found selling toys at the Gare Montparnasse; Martin Scorsese's Hugo tells the story.

fields.Title: Auguste and Louis Lumière
fields.Clue: Brothers from Lyon whose Cinématographe, camera and projector in one, gave the first paid public film screening, at the Grand Café in Paris on 28 December 1895.
fields.Works: Workers Leaving the Lumière Factory; The Arrival of a Train at La Ciotat; The Sprinkler Sprinkled
fields.Notes: L'Arroseur arrosé is often called the first film comedy; they also invented the Autochrome colour plate.

fields.Title: Jacques Demy
fields.Clue: The French director of sung-through, candy-coloured musicals scored by Michel Legrand, one about an umbrella seller's daughter in a Normandy port.
fields.Works: Lola; The Umbrellas of Cherbourg; The Young Girls of Rochefort; Donkey Skin
fields.Notes: Married to Agnès Varda, who filmed his childhood in Jacquot de Nantes.
